Adhering to these conditions is consistent with the thermodynamics, ensuring no heat is dissipated. The principles of fan-out and feedback are essential for logical reversibility. Information reversal logic is applicable in various fields, nanotechnology, and low-power VLSI, optical computing, and quantum computing these are low energy consumption properties. This paper also presents a comparative study of trash outputs, quantum gate costs, and the number of gates used. The designed circuits are implemented and simulated using T-Spice Tools v16.0 software.

articleTitle: Compact and Planar Sinuous Antenna operating in the Wide Band Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the enhancement of a two-arm sinuous antenna’s operational bandwidth through structural modification. The conventional design was altered by introducing slots into the end arcs, to create resonances at the lower frequencies. Simulation results obtained using CST Microwave Studio are presented, with the S-parameter (S11) plots utilized as the primary metric for evaluating the antenna’s performance. The modifications led to a new resonance at 2.4 GHz and 3.5 GHz, effectively extending the antenna’s bandwidth into the lower frequency range. This paper elaborates on the simulation setup, modification process, and resultant changes in the antenna’s performance, offering a wideband operation that could prove beneficial for various communication and radar applications.

articleTitle: Audio Transcription of Meetings and Action Items using LLM’s
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have garnered significant attention as a state-of-art tool for textual data processing and analysis, owing to their unparalleled capacity for generating and comprehending text at a degree of sophistication never seen before [1]. In the realm of meeting management, there are numerous instances of overseeing structured derivatives, leading to missed opportunities for appropriate job delegation and follow-up. This paper describes the use of llama-2 model and technologies like voice transcription, text processing, and action item recognition approaches to streamline the process of audio transcription and precise action item generation from meetings. We have proposed the Action Item Generation System (AIGS) which encompasses real-time and offline audio transcription , text preprocessing and segmentation, action item recognition. Harnessing the advanced text analysis capabilities of LLMs led to notable improvements in distilling pertinent action items for meetings.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Transformer Thermal Performance during Short-circuit test
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Transformer is an important component in the electric grid. Several tests have been defined in relevant standards to ensure reliability of the transformer. Short-circuit test is the one of the critical tests for transformer design verification. Any weakness in design results in the failure of transformer’s short-circuit test. Present paper discusses the thermal performance of the transformer during short-circuit test.Since the transformer experiences excessive amount of current during short-circuit test, transformer winding experiences mainly mechanical stress and thermal stress. Thermal stress shall result in increase in winding temperature. Transformer winding temperature during short-circuit test can be calculated using formulae given in IS/IEC and IEEE. Efforts are made to measure transformer winding temperature during short-circuit test. Comparison is established between calculated and measured transformer winding temperatures during short-circuit test.

articleTitle: Future Finance: Predictive Insights and Chatbot Consultation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The framework has four pillars on which the rest of it is built. Initially, the Stock Analysis sector is a data-driven approach where historical data is broken down into key components to reduce the amount of hidden information. This is as from there onwards the Stock Prediction module is run which applies predictive modeling methodologies to gain market revelations about future market trends and movements with precision which is informed to investors to help them not only to acquire profits but also maintain stability and to gain knowledge on what to expect. The Assystem, complementing smart wearables, utilizes AI Assistance, with forward facing conversational chatbot interface thus creating a natural environment for the users. This AI-enabled assistant provides customized suggestions, up-to-the-minute details, and impeccable representative behavior as it syncs to investors' expectations. Finally, the Market Guider feature offers users the news and updates from the stock market which were curated, enabling them to stay updated with the involved changes. For predictive analysis, we've opted for the LSTM model due to its superior performance compared to other models tested. It achieved an R-squared score of 0.89, indicating strong predictive power, and demonstrated robustness with a cross-validation score of 0.84 on both training and testing datasets. The model was serialized into a Hierarchical Data Format (HDF) file to save runtime operations and facilitate deployment in Streamlit. Through a Streamlit interface, users can input a stock ticker and receive predicted prices generated by the trained LSTM model.

articleTitle: An Automated DeepFake Video Detection System Utilizing Depthwise Separable Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: A DeepFake is a manipulated form of media created using "Deep" learning. Its ability to spread misinformation and threaten personal rights presents a threat. Additional outcomes of DeepFakes include blackmailing, financial scams and harming the reputation of an individual. All these consequences lay emphasis on the significance of its detection. The research aims to detect deepfakes at a more accurate level. The study revolves around Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture. We examined the accuracy of the architecture. The architecture was set up as our base. However high levels of accuracy were not achieved. To enhance accuracy, the research has implemented Xception model architecture and trained it on a huge dataset. Thus we were able to make enhancements in the accuracy. To further achieve a greater precision an optimizer was used. Specifically, "Adam" optimizer was involved in the fine-tuning process at different learning rates. Thus, the highest level of accuracy 99% was achieved.

articleTitle: Clock & Reset Domain Crossing Issues and Verification Techniques for SoC Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The Clock Domain Crossing (CDC) problem is one of the most important problems at the RTL level of a design. The metastability problem is the primary problem with real-time clock designs. Many designs include multiple clock domains where signals must cross from one clock domain to another. Timing constraints help in identifying and managing these crossings to avoid metastability issues and ensure the correct operation of the design. SoCs contain blocks and subsystems running at different clock domains, which create synchronization and metastability issues. When these problems are not resolved early on, the design becomes unreliable and performs poorly. We need to take precautions at the RTL level even though our simulator is unable to verify or observe these problems. Restructuring the design and including the necessary synchronizer cells accomplish this. The goal of this paper is to check for RTL Quality checks such as CDC and RDC to ensure such faults do not occur at later stages of chip development.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Bangus Sorting and Quantifying Machine Using ArUco Marker-Based Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Explores the creation of a machine that effectively sorts and quantifies fish based on precise sizing criteria, contributing to increased customer satisfaction and market reliability. The machine operates by using appropriate camera lighting and the Raspberry Pi platform with ArUco markers for fish sizing detection and conveyor integration. This setup ensures accurate fish recognition and seamless transfer onto a running conveyor belt for sorting. The integration of camera technology enhances the precision of sizing, to integrate of new way of production using image processing. The core functionality of the Fish Sorting and Quantifying Machine lies in its ability to sort fish according to predefined size categories and deposit them into respective containers, streamlining the harvesting processing to store data of the fish measurement to cloud. The results represent a sustainable and eco-friendly solution for fish farming, having 88.41% accuracy using a confusion matrix utilizing advanced technology to provide a reliable, portable, and cost-effective means of sorting and quantifying fish. This innovation enhances fish harvesting processes and promotes environmental consciousness by minimizing reliance on manual labor. This research will delve into the detailed design and development process of the Bangus Sorting and Quantifying Machine, highlighting its technical specifications, operational efficiency, and economic impact on the local aquaculture industry. Through this research and innovation anticipate, solving a critical problem and setting a new standard for the region's efficient and sustainable fish farming practices. Further research and technological advancements in this field hold great potential for improving bangus sorting and quantifying machines and promoting sustainable fish farming practices.

articleTitle: AC-GAN and Machine learning based Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Dysplasia detection system
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Dysplasia is a heart disorder in which the heart muscle is replaced by fatty fibrous tissue. This causes sudden deaths in young men. The proposed novel AC-GAN and machine learning based ARVD detection system focuses mainly on detection of ARVD using ECG signals. This is the first machine learning based approach of detection of ARVD. This system involves creating synthetic ECG data of ARVD using AC-GAN. Since there is no available dataset in the internet, this approach results in large amount of synthetical ECG dataset. The primary characteristics of ARVD include inverted T waves and Epsilon waves at the end of the QRS complex. Various machine learning algorithm, such as the Decision Tree algorithm, Linear discriminant algorithm, Logistic regression algorithm, Naïve Bayes algorithm, RNN LSTM were trained and tested. The RNN LSTM has the highest tested accuracy of 89.2%. And was concluded to be the best fit for the ARVD detection system. The users can upload their ECG data to the web dashboard for real-time prediction.

articleTitle: Exploring Lung Cancer Research Landscape: Bibliometric Analysis Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This bibliometric study examines the emerging area of lung cancer research and its relationship with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) contributions. This research aims to comprehensively analyses and understand the changing landscape of AI and ML applications in the field of lung cancer by methodically reviewing a wide range of academic papers. The study examines several aspects including publishing trends, citation patterns, authorship networks, and theme material. It reveals the significant rise and effect of these technologies in transforming lung cancer diagnosis, treatment, and research methodology. This study utilizes R Studio to do a bibliometric analysis on the field of lung cancer research, specifically examining academic papers obtained from bibliographic databases. By using the functionalities of the R programming language, this research systematically investigates the trends in publications, patterns of citations, and thematic material within the domain of lung cancer. This study employs bibliometric methodologies and utilizes R Studio's analytical capabilities to examine the quantitative characteristics of literature on lung cancer. Through this analysis, valuable insights are gained on the development of research subjects, important publications, authorship networks, and patterns of collaboration. This study offers a detailed analysis of the academic landscape in the field of lung cancer research, using the libraries and functions available in R Studio. It employs quantitative measurements and visual representations to clarify the dynamics and trends that are influencing this area of study.

articleTitle: Night Safety Patrolling Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Night safety patrolling robots have emerged as indispensable assets in enhancing security and surveillance operations in various domains, including urban areas, industrial facilities, and critical infrastructure sites. This abstract provides a comprehensive overview of the advancements in technology and functionality of these robots. This project proposes a comprehensive safety system leveraging advanced technologies for proactive monitoring and response. Central to the system is a Raspberry Pi equipped with a microphone that continuously analyzes audio input to detect distress signals or danger words associated with abnormal human behavior. Upon detection, the system triggers alerts and intimates the Patrol web interface, facilitating swift intervention. In addition to audio monitoring, the system integrates an ESP32 Cam module for continuous 24hour streaming, providing real time visual surveillance. This enables not only the monitoring of surroundings but also serves as a deterrent to potential threats. The combination of audio and visual monitoring ensures comprehensive coverage, enhancing the effectiveness of the safety system. Additionally, the system's architecture is scalable and adaptable, facilitating seamless integration with existing infrastructure and future expansion. Leveraging IoT devices and intelligent algorithms, this women's safety system aims to empower individuals with enhanced security measures, contributing to the creation of safer communities for everyone.

articleTitle: Effective Switch Fault Detection and Classification in Seven-Level Switched capacitor Multilevel Inverter by Using Variable Mode decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are commonly used in industry for various medium and high power applications. However, as the number of switches in an MLI increases, the possibility of faults increases. Ensuring the reliability of MLIs is a critical concern, making effective fault detection and localization methods essential. This paper presents a new method for quickly identifying and locating open switch faults (OCFs) in a single-phase seven-level switched capacitor multilevel inverter (7L-SCMLI), which can triple the voltage output. The method focuses on analyzing the faulty voltage signal produced by the inverter, which contains important information about its operation. To extract useful information from this voltage signal, use a signal processing technique called Variable Mode Decomposition (VMD). VMD breaks the voltage signal into different modes, each highlighting a specific component of the signal. These components are then transformed into singular values to create an analytic signal. This analytic signal helps set a threshold for detecting faults and identifying the faulty switch. Moreover the paper includes detailed analysis and simulation results to validate the effectiveness of this method for the 7L-SCMLI.

articleTitle: MangoStageNet: Computer Vision System for Mango Maturity Stage Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Vision systems have been popularly used in food processing industries to automate the grading and the quality inspection control. The vision systems inspect the various attributes such as color, size, shape, determination of defects. In this work, such features are extracted that determine and analyze the real time data to make decisions about the quality of the mangoes and to sort them accordingly. Acquisition setup is designed to collect the images of mangoes at the unripe stage, preprocessing is applied, color features as in mean values are extracted. These are further fed into the various. The maximum accuracy is achieved by KNN with 97.8 % with minimum misclassifications. A total of 644 under unripe stage , 500 for partially ripe and 244 images of ripe stages were used in the work. Valuation metrics such as Precision recall and F score is also determined.

articleTitle: Early Intervention for Pneumonia: A Deep Learning-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The health and well-being of those who contract pneumonia are seriously at risk due to the disease's rapid spread. A correct biological diagnosis of pneumonia requires the application of multiple diagnostic tools and the evaluation of multiple clinical factors, but these processes are hampered by the dearth of expertise and resources. Based on the findings described here, a web application that classifies patients as having pneumonia or not is being developed using deep learning algorithms. It was intended that this project will result in the development of a web application prototype for neural network-based pneumonia detection. This process is streamlined, and issues such as the optimal number of layers for a neural network are resolved by employing advanced tools such as Create ML, among others, to address and recognize them. We have taken various sample from different places and trained our model with great precision.

articleTitle: Driver Behaviour Classification using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Almost 1.19 million people die in road accidents each year, making them the leading cause of fatalities among children and young adults between the ages of five and twenty-nine. Road safety is therefore a pressing global issue. Road traffic accidents have a substantial financial impact, accounting for roughly 3% of the GDP in the majority of countries. In light of these figures, it is essential to understand driving behavior in order to improve road safety and reduce the number of accidents. Through this paper we present a comprehensive analysis of driver behaviour classification using advanced neural network models. By leveraging the capabilities of deep learning, we aim to capture and analyse the complex patterns and nuances of driver actions particularly classifying driver behaviour into three distinct classes: drowsy, normal, and aggressive. To achieve this classification, we used long short-term memory networks, leveraging its unique capabilities to interpret complex patterns, as for the data source we have used the UAH DriveSet dataset because of its comprehensive feature set, high quality data and real word driving scenarios. The results appear promising, achieving an overall F1 score of 0.98 with Long Short-Term Memory Networks. Through this work, we underscore the importance of leveraging AI and deep learning in tackling the challenges of road safety and driver behaviour analysis.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Reverse Vending Plastic Recycling Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: A reverse vending machine is an automated machine designed to encourage recycling by accepting used plastic bottles and dispensing rewards. These machines are becoming increasingly popular due to the growing awareness of environmental sustainability. The aim of this paper is to design a Reverse Vending Plastic Recycling Machine (RV-PRM) that processes plastic bottles and dispenses coupons based on the mass of recycled plastic. The RV-PRM categorizes plastic bottles into seven bins, each for different types of plastics. When bottles are deposited, the machine uses FPGA technology to accurately calculate the mass of the recycled plastic and determines the number of redeemable coupons. The system also includes UART communication to transfer data from the FPGA to an ESP32 microcontroller, which sends real-time notifications to users' mobile devices. The machine dispenses physical coupons, which can be used at partner retailers, providing an incentive for users to recycle. This innovative solution aims to enhance recycling efforts by combining real-time processing, user engagement, and environmental responsibility.

articleTitle: Real-Time Fake Number Plate Detection And Analysis With Raspberry Pi And Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This project presents an innovative system designed for real-time detection and analysis of counterfeit number plates, combining Raspberry Pi and advanced deep learning technology, notably the You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection algorithm. The primary objective is to bolster security and law enforcement efforts by automating the detection of fraudulent number plates, thereby enhancing traffic monitoring and maintaining the credibility of license plate recognition systems. The project begins with a comprehensive exploration of existing literature, focusing on the state-of-the-art in deep learning algorithms, particularly YOLO, and its applications in object detection tasks. Following this, extensive experimentation and prototyping are conducted to integrate YOLO with the Raspberry Pi platform, ensuring efficient on-board processing for real-time applications. The system's implementation involves the development of a robust pipeline for capturing, preprocessing, and analysing live video streams from surveillance cameras. The YOLO algorithm is then employed to detect and classify number plates within the captured frames, enabling swift identification of counterfeit plates. Our system achieved a detection accuracy of over 90% across diverse lighting conditions and plate variations.

articleTitle: Effect of High-K Dielectrics and Metal Gate Work Function on the Performance and Reliability of Finfets
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In this work, we present an analysis of the electrical characteristics of a 3D silicon-on-insulator (SOI) FinFET having a gate length of 8nm. Technology computer-aided design (TCAD) based analysis has been used to obtain FinFETs with reliable performance. The simulation results show an improvement in the on-state current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>), and improved leakage current for different high-κ materials such as HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Additionally, other performance and reliability parameters such as I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> ratio, transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), subthreshold slope (SS), and drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) have also been analyzed. For a better understanding of the simulation results, a brief analysis of the effect of the metal gate workfunction is also presented. It has been found that an increase in workfunction leads to improvements in leakage current, thus enhancing the device’s reliability. However, the threshold voltage was found to be increasing with the metal gate workfunction which adversely affects the switching characteristics. Hence a proper trade-off is required to achieve a balance between performance and reliability of FinFETs. This work is expected to provide a valuable addition to designing FinFETs with optimized device performance as well as reliability.

articleTitle: School Automation System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The objective of this project was to create a responsive application for the school automation system.This system has features like staff and student information, attendance tracking, and a chat window for instructor and parent engagement.The goal of this project is to computerize paper activities and automate tasks within the system.This approach enhances communication between instructors, parents, and students as well as the administrative workload.This application has improved the productivity, organization, and collaboration of the educational community.It consists of the admin and user modules.Exam cell users can modify students’ pass/fail statuses in the database; administrator-controlled admin modules can add or update student data; and user-controlled user modules can add or update student data.Less data duplication is likely because the system stores information about teachers and students, and it is centralized.As the number of students increases, so does the amount of data that needs to be kept. This has led to a need for a controlled, compact framework that can be triggered with a single window click, hence reducing paperwork.Schools can easily use this system, which serves as a centralized database and application, from any place as long as they have the correct login credentials

articleTitle: DeepWeed: A Dynamically Adaptive Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Efficient Weed Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This work introduces DeepWeed, a lightweight deep-learning model inspired by the VGG16 architecture for image-based weed classification. Leveraging transfer learning and L2 regularization, DeepWeed aims to achieve high accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Our study evaluated the model’s performance on a dataset of five weed species. While an initial accuracy of 73.6% was achieved without data augmentation and L2 regularization, incorporating these techniques significantly improved, reaching an accuracy of 92.4 %. This increase highlights the effectiveness of data augmentation and L2 regularization in enhancing model performance. DeepWeed’s combination of high accuracy and computational efficiency suggests its potential as a practical tool for weed classification in agricultural applications, potentially contributing to improved farm management and reduced environmental impact.

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for Automated Mushroom Disease Diagnosis using CNN and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This research study has fully examined a classification model to detect several mushroom ailments, including a healthy class, based on Convolutional Neural Networks and Random Forest algorithms. The study considers six mushroom ailments, namely Wet Bubble Disease, Green Mold Disease, Cobweb Disease, Bacterial Blotch, and Mushroom Fly Infestation, based on precision, recall, F1-score, support, support percentage, and accuracy for analysis. It is worth noting that the precision score ranges from 95.90% to 97.21% indicating the accuracy of positive predictions for each ailment class. Similarly, the recall score ranges from 95.80% to 97.32%, representing the model’s ability to capture true positive cases. In addition, the F1-score represents a balance between accuracy and recall demonstrating a performance variation in different ailment classes is still good, ranging from 96.10% to 97.13%. The model has an overall weighted average accuracy of 99%, indicating the model can be robustly and efficiently applied to classify mushroom diseases. Analysis of the support percentages provided information on the relative distribution of each class case in the sample. Based on these performances, it can be concluded that the model of the CNN and Random Forest plays a crucial role in the automated disease diagnosis of the mushroom industry to pave the way for enhanced disease control and sustainable mushroom production techniques.

articleTitle: Experimentation Using GEI and AFDEI for Person Recognition with PCA, LDA, and Ensemble Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This paper investigates person recognition using GAIT patterns, focusing on Gait Energy Image (GEI) and Accumulative Frame Difference Energy Image (AFDEI). Feature extraction was performed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and a fusion of PCA-LDA. Various classifiers, including Logistic Regression, NB, SVM, MLP, Random Forest, and KNN, were assessed. Results showed that KNN with Principal Component Analysis -fusion features achieved 73.5% accuracy, while Random Forest with LDA-GAIT Energy Image features achieved 77.4%. SVM and Naive Bayesian with Principal Component Analysis-Linear Discriminant Analysis fusion features achieved 76.0%. Ensemble techniques, including Adaboost, Gradient Boosting, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, were also tested. The highest accuracies were 67.9% for SVM-Adaboost with Principal Component Analysis-GAIT Energy Image features, 70.4% for Random Forest-Adaboost with Linear Discriminant Analysis-GAIT Energy Image features, and 75.9% for Logistic Regression-Adaboost with PCA-LDA Analysis fusion features. This study underscores the significance of feature extraction techniques and the selection of appropriate machine learning classifiers in enhancing the accuracy of person recognition systems based on GAIT patterns, providing valuable insights for future research and practical implementations.

articleTitle: Leveraging CNN-SVM Hybrid Models for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy in Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by motor and non-motor manifestations. The management and treatment of the condition require accurate diagnosis and early identification of the infection. This paper outlines a novel deep-learning model that integrates CNNs and SVMs to improve the classification of the photos into five types of Parkinson’s disease. The model attempts to enhance the computerized diagnosis of the illogical clusters of diseases by applying a set of 300 pictures, including 200 images of sick persons and 100 pictures of healthy persons. The photos, for instance, underwent a rigorous normalization and data augmentation process to optimize the learning process and model robustness. On this split, the model started training 70% of the data for training purposes, 15% for validation, and 15% for testing. The results proved to be very convincing. The results of experiments show that the model is relatively accurate, with an overall accuracy of 96%. The precision rates vary between 82, and as low as 71%. 64% to 92. 0% to 63%, while the average recall rate varies from 81. 59% to 93. they are 70% for the sel categoillnesses that have people. F1-scores obtained ranged from 82: 11% and 91. Thus, the algorithm achieves a balanced performance in terms of accuracy and recall, which is 16%. These measurements shall verify the model’s ability to significantly aid in the early and accurate diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease, augmenting future treatment strategies and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches in Agri-tech: Federated Learning Models for Disease Detection in Papaya Leaves
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Diseases particularly affect the leaves of papaya plants significantly affect yield as they reduce both quantity and quality. It is, therefore, important for agriculture to seek ways of solving the issues of fast and accurate methods of disease diagnosis. To achieve the goals of this work, which is the classification of the four main diseases affecting the papaya tree and its leaves, this paper proposes a new scheme that is based on federated learning, CNN, and the FedAvg algorithm. In contrast to most known approaches, by working with six different geographic sites to compute six individual models that contain locally relevant data, the presented federated learning scheme allows for fully efficient, scalable, and protective computation without the need for data unification, with sound indicators of 91% accuracy, which is also commonly known as precision, 90% recall, which is also acknowledged as sensitivity and 90 F-Measure. The overall response accuracy to the illness categorization was 92%, of which the F1-score indicated that this model was very effective, especially at 5% F1-score. In addition to minimizing major privacy issues, the amount of displayed data was reduced to a level in which the federated strategy helped decrease training bandwidth by as much as 76% for different models. Due to these features, the proposed approach is most suitable for actual agricultural environments where data privacy and network performance are paramount. Our study shows that federated learning can revolutionize agricultural disease management due to its capability of offering timely and precise interventions.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach to Climate Prediction: Neural Networks and Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The use of the neural networks, fuzzy logic, and ANFIS (Artificial Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System) integrated models to examine the forecasting of climate condition is the objective of the research study. The aim is to enhance the accuracy of climate forecasting and bring insightful data for decision-makers who will have to deal with the problems of climate change through the evaluation of present computer models. The article is built on the basis of the FNN architecture for weather classification, the dataset of which was downloaded from Kaggle and consisted of eleven classifications of 6862 weather photos. Moreover, the ANFIS (which is a blend of fuzzy logic and neural networks for automatically generating rules) is particular in that it facilitates the fuzzy-rule based classification. The research employs the checks and verifications of the FNN and ANFIS models through assessing their accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score values. The merged model significantly outperforms the individual models, as evident in the high 94% accuracy, 96% precision, 92% recall, and 94% f1-score results. The integrated model is an indispensable instrument in policy-making and adaptation measures definition in the context of climate change, as evidenced by its exceptional talent in tracking climate variations, as emphasized by its 0.92 CRSI. The results showed the central role of the combined use of neural networks and the fuzzy logic methods in climate prediction, hence the need for further research to increase the models’ scalability and tackle complex climate dynamics corollary.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Optimum Thickness and ZT values by using Material Properties and Heat Transfer Coefficient by varying Thermal Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The recommended work is to enhance the Optimum Thickness and ZT values by using Thermoelectric power by varying Thermal Resistance using coefficient of heat transfer and properties of the material. The coefficient of heat transfer and properties of the material methods are implemented to improve the Optimum Thickness and ZT values by varying Thermal Resistance of Thermoelectric power. Two sets are taken into account where, set 1 is Heat Transfer Coefficient and set 2 is Material Properties. Each set comprises two samples and a cumulative sample size of 10. The G power calculation resulting in 0.8.The Optimum Thickness and ZT values will experience enhancement through variation of the Thermal Resistance in Optimizing thermoelectric power through artificial intelligence techniques. The SPSS analysis yields a p-value of 0.159 for the obtained independent sample t-test values. The Heat Transfer Coefficient in Optimum Thickness and ZT values is (3.2957) compared to the Material Properties is (4.02562) at the Thermal Resistance range of (210-300). The max range of Optimum Thickness and ZT values is 4.02562 T=300(K-m2/W). From this work it is noticed that the Material Properties (4.02562) performed much better than Heat Transfer Coefficient (3.2957) in Optimum Thickness and ZT values by Improvement of Thermoelectric power under varying Thermal Resistance.

articleTitle: Grid-connected 300 kW PV system with Improved Maximum PowerPoint Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: An analysis of the design and implementation of a 300 kW PV system that is linked to the grid and uses the MPPT algorithm developed by Perturb and Observe (P&O). The MPPT algorithm is an essential component of PV systems. Its primary function is to ensure effective operation by continuously modifying the operating point of the PV modules. This allows the modules to collect the highest amount of electricity possible from the varying solar irradiation circumstances. In this study, the P&O technique is used since it is simple and effective at tracking the maximum power point (MPP) and it doesn't require a lot of computer resources. In order to test how well the proposed PV system works in various environments, it is modeled and simulated using MATLAB software tools. In order to maximize power extraction from PV modules while ensuring a steady grid connection, the simulation results show that the P&O MPPT algorithm is effective. The study also delves into how system characteristics like temperature and irradiance level affect the efficiency and performance of the MPPT. The results give light on how to optimize and construct large-scale PV systems that are connected to the grid and use MPPT algorithms to increase energy yield while integrating with the grid.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Assistive Iot Based Flood and Disaster Rescue Management System Using ESP8266 WiFi Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: More and more, it seems like every year or virtually every year, floods hit various regions of the globe. Recent technological developments have facilitated the acquisition of solutions for these natural catastrophes. A good example of a technology that brings us closer to the web is the IoT, or Internet of Things. This study presents an Internet of Things (IoT)-based system for flood detection and catastrophe prevention. This uses its on-board sensors to make educated guesses about things like humidity, temperature, and water flow; it then uploads the information in actual time to the cloud services, where users may examine it using an application for their smartphones. In this paper, a new disaster recovery system is introduced called Artificial Intelligence based Rescue Management Model (AIRMM), in which it is cross-validated with the conventional GPRS based Flood Monitoring Model (GPRSFMM) to evaluate the efficiency of the proposed scheme. The suggested Internet of Things (IoT) system analyzes earthquake and flood data in real-time, allowing authorities to keep tabs on areas hit by natural disasters. In this article, we take a look at the Flood and Earthquake Monitoring System, which can help us keep an eye on high-risk locations for earthquakes and floods in real time while keeping an eye on costs and safety precautions. Additionally, the suggested system notifies the proper authorities whenever it detects a person in the vicinity. The suggested system's design incorporates sensors into the microcontroller NodeMCU WiFi Module and the Internet of Things platform so that the uploaded data from the sensors may be examined and seen.

articleTitle: Empowering Security: Machine Learning Solutions for Detecting Brute Force Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: It is essential to identify brute force attacks, which are a common type of cyber security threat, to protect networks and desktops against unauthorised entry. Previous rule-based methods frequently face difficulties in adjusting to the changing strategies and intricacies of contemporary attacks. This paper presents a machine learning(ML) approach to detect brute-force attacks by utilising predictive modelling and anomaly detection technology. The technique seeks to detect suspicious activity that is symptomatic of brute force attacks by analysing trends in unsuccessful logins, user behaviours, and network traffic. Utilise a range of ML algorithms, such as Logistic Regression (LR), Naive Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT), and K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), to train predictive models on labelled datasets containing past attack data. In addition, investigate feature design strategies, model parameters, and assessment metrics to enhance the effi-ciency of the detection system. By conducting experiments and evaluating real-world datasets, want to prove the efficiency and scalability of the suggested method in effectively detecting brute force attacks while reducing the occurrence of false positives. The findings emphasise the capacity of ML techniques to strengthen cybersecurity measures and reduce the threats presented by brute-force attacks in the current digital environment. The NB, KNN, and LR classifiers have accuracy rates of 87.51%, 99.80%, and 95.55%, respectively. The DT classifier achieves the greatest accuracy rate of 99.96%.

articleTitle: Development of Women's Safety System Using Iot and Taser Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The women safety device is an innovative IoT-based safety system designed to monitor key physiological parameters, such as heartbeat and EEG, and coupled with a panic switch, GSM, GPS, and IoT modules. This system provides real-time monitoring of vital signs, enabling swift detection of distress or emergencies. In the event of abnormal conditions or manual activation through the panic switch, the system triggers immediate alerts via the GSM module to predefined contacts, accompanied by real-time GPS location tracking. The IoT module facilitates seamless connectivity, enabling remote monitoring through a centralized platform. The women safety device prioritizes emergency response, user privacy, data security, and compliance with regulatory standards. It aims to empower individuals and contribute to a safer and more secure environment for women. A GPS-built women's sanctuary system with dual security elements is proposed to help overcome this issue. A woman can press the prepared switch when she is in danger and needs to act to protect her. When a woman, child, or senior is harassed or in distress, the gadget notifies the family and appropriate authorities of the woman's current position. An electric shock generator incorporated into the panic button on the gadget is a peculiar feature. In conclusion, the women safety device is a comprehensive solution to ensure the safety and well-being of women in today society.

articleTitle: Audio Classification through MFCC features using RNN algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) algorithm, is renowned for its effectiveness in object localization and classification tasks within the realm of computer vision. This study combines RNN capabilities with the analysis of Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients(MFCC) features, which have demonstrated effectiveness in capturing unique audio signal characteristics. Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) serve as a compact representation of the spectral content of audio signals, enabling the identification of distinctive features crucial for detecting anomalies introduced during the generation of deepfake audio. The Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) algorithm is applied to these MFCC features. RNN excels in tasks such as image recognition, object detection, and semantic segmentation. Previous research in the field of audio forensics has explored various methodologies for detecting manipulated audio content. While some approaches focus on signal processing techniques, others employ machine learning algorithms. MFCCs have consistently demonstrated their efficacy in capturing audio features relevant to authenticity. The proposed approach enhances the detection of fake audio, a critical challenge in the era of advanced digital media manipulation. By combining the strengths of MFCC features and the RNN algorithm, the model aims to learn and identify intricate patterns associated with genuine audio, enabling accurate differentiation between authentic and manipulated audio sources. By adapting RNN to analyze MFCC features, the model gains the capability to discern intricate patterns associated with genuine audio, thereby distinguishing between authentic and manipulated audio sources.

articleTitle: Implementation Of 5-Level Cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Multilevel inverters have gained popularity in recent years due to their capacity to produce high-quality output voltages with lower harmonic distortion and switching losses than conventional two-level inverters. The Cascaded H-bridge configuration is unique among multilevel inverter topologies due to its simplicity, scalability, modularity, and low component count, making it an appealing choice for a variety of applications such as renewable energy systems, motor drives, and grid-tied inverters. This paper presents the design, implementation, and performance analysis of a 5-level Cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter. The implementation presented in this study serves as an educational tool, supplementing theoretical knowledge for students and enabling analysis of performance parameters.

Author Keywords: Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (MOSFET)

articleTitle: Automated Weed Detection and Removal using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Precision agriculture uses cutting-edge technology to improve farming operations, increase crop yields, and reduce resource use. This study focuses on developing an autonomous weed and crop detection system that leverages the cutting-edge You Only Look Once (YOLO) algorithm.The purpose is to equip farmers with a real-time solution to identify and distinguish crops fromweeds in agricultural fields. The process entails creating a well-annotated dataset with photos of both crops and weeds. A pre- trained YOLO model, such as YOLOv3 or YOLOv4, is chosen and fine-tuned with the annotated dataset. The YOLO configuration file is changed to meet the unique crop and weed detection needs. The training procedure continues until adequate convergence is obtained. The trained YOLO model is then connectedwith agricultural equipment, such as drone-mounted cameras or other sensing devices, allowing for real- time detection in the field. Post-processing techniques are used to improve detection results while minimizing false positives. Decision-making algorithms are developed to direct activities based on the detected crops and weeds, allowing for focused interventions such as precision herbicide administration.

Author Keywords: Autonomous weed and crop detection system

articleTitle: Stock and Cryptocurrency Price Prediction using SVM and LSTM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Businesses can endeavour to raise money through multiple avenues. One such would be to realize the value of other business success. Purchasing and selling ownership shares in publicly traded corporations on the stock market. These prices are influenced by various factors such as investor sentiment, economic demography, and company performance. To purchase when low and sell when high or to cash in on company dividends both profit investors. The Stock Market is the backbone of many investment portfolios and impacts the global economy. The concept of data handling and interpreting data has been reshaped by machine learning[13]. This allows for computers to extract large volumes of data, judge, or predict without requiring explicit programming. This abstract covers a broad review of machine learning algorithms and their applications in different fields. A few examples include supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning. In supervised learning, a model is focused on labelled data to train it to predict or categorise new data. This project uses Random Forest, LSTM, and SVM to predict the price of stocks and cryptocurrencies. The prediction graphs can be viewed on the Streamlit website. The project is anticipated to have a 97.6% accuracy Rate.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Model Merging LOF and iForest Algorithms for Insider Threats Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Insider threats are among the most difficult challenges in cybersecurity, often leading to substantial losses for organizations. Insider threats remain a well-researched area of cybersecurity, with continuous development of detection techniques to combat this persistent challenge. This research investigates the effectiveness of various anomaly detection algorithms, specifically focusing on the Locality Outlier Factor (LOF) and Isolation Forest (IF) algorithms. The study conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis to evaluate their performance in identifying anomalous data points. By delving into the strengths and weaknesses of each approach, the research aims to provide valuable insights into choosing the most suitable algorithm for different anomaly detection applications. This paper goes beyond individual anomaly detection algorithms by proposing a novel hybrid model that leverages the strengths of both Locality Outlier Factor (LOF) and Isolation Forest (IF). This innovative approach demonstrably outperforms both standalone methods in detecting insider threats, achieving a remarkable accuracy of 99%.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Image Filters in Facial Detection through Different Classification Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In the present work, we have analyzed the effect of applying different filters in face detection through different classification methods. For the purpose, we have created different datasets: first dataset consists of 1600 different unfiltered images of eight students with 200 images of each student and second dataset consists of 8000 filtered images using a mix of filters with 1000 images of each student. Then we created five additional datasets, each dataset created by applying a single filter. Five filters namely blur, cut-out, mosaic, noise and shear are used for the present study. Six different algorithms CNN, Random Forest, SVM, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, KNN, and Logistic Regression were applied and results of unfiltered image dataset and filtered image dataset using a mix of filters have been compared. We found a little improvement in the accuracy in the case of KNN and CNN and a little decline in accuracy of other algorithms applied to filtered dataset created using a mix of filters. The significance of difference between the two results is checked through paired t-test. Based on paired t-test, we conclude that filters in images, in general, do not have much effect in face detection through different classification algorithms. The results of unfiltered dataset and individual filtered datasets show that there is a significant difference in results between the unfiltered dataset and blur filtered dataset, others being identical. This indicates that the filter ‘blur’ has some effect in face detection and other has no significant effect.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network and Regression Analysis Techniques for Campus Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The process of estimating future electrical load requirements through the analysis of historical consumption data is termed electrical load forecasting. This paper presents a medium-term load forecasting study utilizing a dataset obtained from the Pimpri Chinchwad College of Engineering and Research, Pune, India. The study encompasses a comparative analysis of two distinct forecasting methodologies detailed herein.The dataset, despite its uniqueness, was subjected to two analytical approaches: regression analysis and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models. These were chosen to ascertain their efficacy in generating reliable medium-term load forecasts. The evaluation of these methods was primarily based on two statistical metrics: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE).The outcomes of the comparative analysis delineated a marked superiority of the ANN model, which exhibited lower error rates with MAPE and RMSE values at 0.0285 and 1.124, respectively. The ANN’s robustness in handling diverse load data patterns significantly contributed to its enhanced performance over the traditional regression approach.The findings reinforce the ANN model’s higher accuracy and reliability in medium-term load forecasting. Consequently, this model provides a superior framework for electric load prediction, which is crucial for efficient energy management and planning. The superior performance of the ANN model advocates for its integration into future research and application within power system design. This study serves as a benchmark for advancing load forecasting methodologies, promoting enhanced accuracy and reliability. Further research could explore the integration of more complex algorithms and hybrid models to push the boundaries of forecasting accuracy. Enhancements in data quality, variability, and volume could also potentially refine the forecasting outputs. These advancements will be pivotal for developing adaptive, robust, and efficient power systems capable of meeting dynamic demands and operational challenges.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Transformation of HR: Enhancing Recruitment, Training, and Employee Retention
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The paper introduces a new AI solution known as the Resume Analyzer which is developed to support HR functions through recruitment, training and job sustainability with the K-Nearest Neighbors. The Resume Analyzer analyses text data from job adverts as well as resumes before giving candidates scores based on how well they meet specific requirements in their respective fields hence making it easier for one to sift through many applicants quickly. After testing on various datasets which showed that its accuracy rate was 97.4%, 97% in terms of precision and F1 score of 86%. Methodology consists of meticulous training across 25 job domains using a large number of resumes to ensure robustness and applicability in different industries. Not only does this AI-driven method speed up recruitment processes, but it also boosts job-candidate matching thus leading to long-term job placements. It has various HR applications that make it useful for recruitment purposes as well as talent management, staff training activities or workforce planning; hence scalability is guaranteed in these areas. The system is a good tool for companies that want to improve their human resource strategies by ensuring that they are efficient and effective in managing staff.

articleTitle: Defending Authenticity: Real-Time Signature Verification with Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Deep learning-based signature verification uses sophisticated neural network topologies to verify signatures. Deep learning models may be trained to discriminate between authentic and falsified signatures with a high degree of accuracy by utilizing methods such as vgg, xceptionmodels and Transfer Learning. These models are made to examine the complex characteristics and patterns found in signatures, which allows them to identify minute variations that could point to fraud. Deep learning methods provide a reliable and effective way to handle jobs involving the verification of signatures by utilizing large libraries and complex algorithms. The implementation of deep learning techniques for image processing and classification tasks, which can be adapted for signature verification applications. By preprocessing signature images, extracting relevant features, and training deep learning models on labeled data, the system can learn to differentiate between authentic and forged signatures effectively. Using deep learning involves the development and deployment of neural network models that can accurately authenticate signatures by analyzing their unique characteristics and patterns.

articleTitle: The Future of Cyber Defence: ML and DL Enhanced Firewalls for Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Given the increasing frequency of network-based threats, there is a critical need for robust intrusion detection systems (IDS) to safeguard digital assets. Traditional rule-based IDS often struggle to counter emerging cyber threats, highlighting the demand for more adaptive solutions. This study introduces the Next Generation Firewall (NGFW), an advanced firewall system enhanced by machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques. By integrating ML algorithms like Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests, and Deep Neural Networks (DNN) with DL models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), the NGFW significantly improves detection flexibility, effectiveness, and accuracy. Our comprehensive literature review demonstrates the substantial impact of ML and DL on IDS performance. The NGFW's approach includes systematic data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction, and rigorous model evaluation using metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall. Experimental results show that CNNs excel in detecting malicious activities with minimal false positive rates. Real-world testing further validates the NGFW's capacity to strengthen cybersecurity measures. The classification report reveals impressive performance, with precision, recall, and F1-scores exceeding 97% in each category and an overall accuracy of 97.29%. These results underscore the potential of ML and DL to advance intelligent cybersecurity solutions and enhance the reliability of intrusion detection systems.

articleTitle: Malware Attack Detection Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Conventional signature-driven detection techniques are becoming less and less effective in protecting computer systems and networks due to the increasing complexity and diversity of malware threats. Therefore, the need for sophisticated methods that consistently detect malicious software is essential. As machine learning (ML) can scan vast datasets and identify intricate patterns, it has become a potential method for detecting malware. This research article presents a thorough analysis of the use of machine learning methods in malware attack detection. This research begins by discussing into the basic ideas behind malware and how cyber dangers are changing. It then explores different machine learning methods used for malware detection, such as supervised, and unsupervised learning approaches. The method of selecting features and the importance of feature engineering in improving machine learning models’ ability to identify malware are covered in the article.Additionally, the study assesses the effectiveness of various machine learning methods, including Logistic regression, Random Forest, and Neural Network. To evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of each method with regard to scalability, computational efficiency, and detection accuracy, comparative studies are carried out.

articleTitle: Development of Control for Low Flow Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Low-flow control applications are critical for shower systems and various industrial applications. These applications are indispensable due to the precise flow and temperature conditions required by many processes, which make them essential for achieving desired results. Present flow control applications vary in complexity, and some require skilled installation and maintenance, which can be expensive and sensitive. Traditional control methods can be limiting, resulting in heavy and bulky structures. This paper presents a novel mathematical modeling and advanced control strategy to control low flow applications. The presented simulation results, which include PID and fuzzy logic controllers, demonstrate that smooth control can be achieved by varying various parameters in combination. These findings offer valuable insights into the development of control strategies for low flow applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes through Machine Learning and Logistic Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: A persistent illness Diabetes might become an international health emergency. Diabetes mellitus, also known as diabetes, is typified by high blood sugar levels. Being among the worst diseases in the world, it is also spreading more and more. Diabetes can be diagnosed by a variety of traditional techniques as well as chemical and physical testing. Techniques used in data science may benefit other scientific disciplines since they throw new insight on pressing problems. Machine learning is a contemporary area of data science that focuses on how computers learn from experience. This paper develops and assesses a machine learning model to predict gestational diabetes using a large set of data of physiological markers and health features This study uses 768 examples to create and test a binary classification model to predict gestational diabetes utilizing characteristics including pregnancy, blood pressure, insulin levels, BMI, age, and family history. Class '1' diabetes has 0.72 accuracy, while class '0' has 0.79. However, diabetic recall is substantially poorer (0.55) than non-diabetic (0.89), indicating many missed positives. F1-scores (0.83 for class '0' and 0.63 for class '1') indicate the model's diabetes detection shortcomings and the need for prediction improvement.

articleTitle: Classification of Various Diseases in Tomato Crops using Neural Network Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Tomatoes are an important crop worldwide, playing a substantial role in the agriculture sector. However, they are sensitive to various diseases that can affect yield, quality of crops, and former economic stability. This research focused on developing a system for classifying tomato diseases based on leaf images using machine learning and image processing techniques. Our research utilized convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to predict and classify tomato diseases, employing a dataset from Kaggle containing five disease classes and one healthy leaf class. Our optimized models were tested, showing inconsistent accuracy in detecting and classifying five different tomato diseases. Apart from that, MobileNet and VGG-19 models showed prominent performance and achieved an accuracy of 93.87% compared to other models such as VGG16 and a Customized CNN.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity through Anomaly Detection in Network Traffic Using Convolutional Neural Networks: A Sustainable Development Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: A major problem in the digital era, cybersecurity touches many different industries and is strongly related to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) including infrastructure and industrial innovation (SDG 9) and peace, justice, and strong institutions (SDG 16). Modern solutions are needed because conventional anomaly detection techniques often fail as cyber threats become more sophisticated and frequent. An original method for anomaly detection in network traffic using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) is presented in this article. We train and assess our model using the extensive range of normal and abnormal network events included in the CICIDS2017 dataset. We report a remarkable accuracy of 93.64% for our CNN-based approach, far better than conventional methods. This method not only makes cybersecurity measures stronger but also encourages innovation in accordance with SDG 9 and resilient infrastructure. Moreover, it helps robust institutional frameworks by efficiently identifying and reducing cyber dangers, thus advancing SDG 16. Performance curves, accuracy, recall, F1 score, and confusion matrices are among the many carefully examined and shown outcomes. Our results emphasize the need of including sophisticated machine learning methods—deep learning in particular—into cybersecurity architectures. Creation of safe and sustainable digital ecosystems depends critically on this integration. The ability of our model to precisely identify network abnormalities emphasizes how CNNs may revolutionize cybersecurity procedures. This study argues for the ongoing investigation and use of deep learning approaches to tackle the ever-increasing cybersecurity issues, therefore promoting the accomplishment of important SDGs and guaranteeing the stability and security of digital infrastructure.

articleTitle: Symptom-Based Disease Prediction Framework Integrated with Django and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In healthcare, spotting diseases early is crucial. This project uses machine learning to predict diseases based on symptoms. We used CSV files, which contain datasets with lots of symptoms and diseases. Our fancy model, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Sequential Model with SoftMax activation function, looks at these symptoms to find patterns and identify diseases early. We’re trying to predict all sorts of diseases like Fungal infection, Allergy¸ Diabetes, etc. covering a wide range of health issues. By studying different symptoms like Itching, Skin rash, Nodal skin Eruptions, etc. our model learns how to tell disease possibility from it. After lots of training and testing, our model can predict diseases with an impressive accuracy of 97.66\%. But it’s not just about finding diseases – we want to give doctors a tool that can also help them understand how diseases progress and what might happen next. To make this process accessible and user-friendly, we have designed a user interface (UI) that simplifies interaction with the model. Through this interface, users can input their symptoms, and the model provides predictions about potential diseases. Moreover, users have the option to connect with healthcare professionals for further guidance and treatment. This project breaks new ground by utilizing symptom-based data for disease prediction, aiming to detect illnesses earlier and expedite treatment. Through the integration of advanced technology, comprehensive symptom data, and a user-friendly interface (UI), our goal is to enhance healthcare accessibility and outcomes for all.

Author Keywords: Healthcare data modeling Django web framework

articleTitle: Smart and Sustainable: Verilog HDL Integration in Laundry Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Efficient Laundry machine control systems are essential for modern appliances. In this study, we explored the use of Verilog Hardware Description Language (HDL) to improve laundry machine control systems. Our study, which is based on a finite state machine (FSM) model, attempts to improve laundry cycles and user interactions. Unlike traditional laundry machines with limited controls and fixed timers, our design introduces multiple laundry modes tailored to different fabric types, each with specific timers for user customization. Our design highlights the integration of load sensors to detect laundry weight, assisting users in selecting appropriate modes and preventing operation if the load exceeds a set threshold. A temperature sensor ensures the water temperature is maintained as per user input, optimizing cleaning efficiency and energy use. Additionally, the design includes a safety feature allowing users to pause the laundry process by opening the lid to add extra load at any stage, ensuring user safety. The smart functionality of our laundry machine is driven by its adaptable modes with dedicated timers, enhanced safety mechanisms, and sustainability features through sensor integration. These advancements collectively contribute to a more intelligent, user-friendly, and energy-efficient laundry machine design.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Financial Portfolios: A New Approach to Adaptive Strategy Development
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In today’s world of rapidly fluctuating financial markets, static portfolio management approaches prove to be inadequate to deal with complex conditions and fluctuations. This paper aims to understand the practical implications of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for building smart and self-sufficient trading strategies for the financial portfolio. Thus, we employ and examine three well-known DRL methods, namely DQN, PPO, and TD3 for enhancing the portfolio’s performance. For performance evaluation, we use a comprehensive dataset of historical price data and other financial ratios accumulated over 10 years. This study shows that DRL models have higher performance as compared to conventional methods: Markowitz mean-variance optimization and simple benchmark equal-weighted portfolio, and Machine learning techniques: SVM and RF. Among the DRL models considered here, TD3 recorded the highest total return of 145.8%, the highest risk-adjusted returns with a Sharpe ratio of 1.40, the maximum drawdown of 11.8%, and the lowest volatility of 11.5%. These outcomes reveal the efficiency and stability of the application of DRL approaches in financial portfolio management. This research adds to the expanding literature in financial technology, which presents a new and efficient strategy for improving portfolio management for investors and financial institutions using better computational algorithms.

Author Keywords: Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients

articleTitle: Resolvio: User Feedback and Complaint Analysis using ML
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In urban landscapes worldwide, public toilets have historically been neglected, resulting in subpar sanitation conditions. There is a recognition for the urgent need to revolutionize the perception and upkeep of public toilets. Public toilets are marred by issues like dirty washrooms, broken amenities and availability of amenities such as sanitary pads, hand wash etc. This research paper delves into the positive shifts initiated by local governing bodies, exploring how proactive strategies are turning public toilets into well-maintained. Leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), our project applies advanced technologies to analyze user feedback, sentiment, and images. Through our innovative platform "Resolvio - User Feedback and Complaint Analysis", we aim to revolutionize public toilet maintenance, making them cleaner, safer, and more responsive to community needs, thus contributing to a brighter and sanitary urban future.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Security in ECG Classification: The Federated Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This research paper looks at the ability of the Federated Learning approach to accomplish the classification of Electrocardiogram (ECG) data with a focus on how it ensures the enhanced security of data even as it enhances the classification efficiency. Using an ECG synthetic dataset to compare the performance of FL with the two classic centralized learning methods, the paper uses a simulated network of 10 nodes equivalent to a healthcare system. The evaluation of accuracy in the Federated Learning setup gave an average classification accuracy of 90%, slightly lower than the 92% displayed in the central model, validating its effectiveness. Specifically, no data breaches were incurred under the decentralized approach of Florida, while two have been reported under the centralized strategy, which stresses a higher security establishment. Besides, correlation analysis and heat maps are used in the research where one obtains high positive results for proving the relationship between the FL model’s accuracy and system efficiency. From the findings of this study, it is clear that Federated Learning provides adequate protection for health information while promising fast processing and accurate results. Thus, the study demonstrates that the FL framework has tremendous possibilities in becoming an innovative approach to handling personal medical data; these findings have significant consequences for healthcare organizations that strive to enhance personal data protection and fulfil the requirements of data protection legislation. Future work includes evaluating the proposed system on real-world applications and incorporating more confidential encryption schemes to enhance the security of Federated Learning frameworks.

articleTitle: Amalgam Based Multilingual Text Summarization For Devanagari Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The absence of efficient text summarizers for languages based on the Devanagari script like Hindi, Marathi and Sanskrit exhibit a conspicuous void in field of literature being devoid of the linguistic masterpieces. This study introduces a customized Multilingual Text Summarizer for Marathi and Hindi that makes use of a combination Python’s TextRank algorithm and Bag of Words (BOW) algorithm alongside extractive summarization techniques using a flask web application. By preserving the meaning and extracting most used words and sentences, our approach yields accurate summaries. The dataset used contains news articles and their summaries for testing our model. Empirical assessments using ROUGE approach confirms its efficiency in generating effective summaries with over 88% score.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Decision-Making: An Automated Approach for Manufacturing Companies in E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This manuscript explores the automation of customer review analysis on e-commerce platforms from different manufacturing firms. It examines the difficulties in sentiment analysis, quality control, data extraction, and ethical issues. The study stresses data privacy and ethical usage while acknowledging constraints including prejudice and language barriers. The suggested approach helps businesses make decisions and develop their products by offering insightful data on consumer perception and product performance. In the big data era, it provides enterprises with a framework to leverage automation for comparison analysis. The results obtained proves the efficacy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Predicting Drinking Behaviour based on Physiological Signals using Ensemble Boosting Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This paper focuses on Machine learning (ML) classifier-based analysis which offers a promising approach to classify drinking behavior. This study compared four boosting algorithms (Gradient Boosting (GB), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Adaptive Boosting (ADB), and Histogram Boosting (HB)) for classifying drinkers and non-drinkers using a dataset with individual characteristics and physiological signals. All algorithms achieved good accuracy, with GB and HB showing the best balance between training and testing performance. Additionally, GB, XGB, and HB achieved a high AUC (0.82), demonstrating their effectiveness in classifying drinking behavior. This study highlights the potential of ML for analyzing physiological body signals to classify drinking behavior.

articleTitle: IoT Security in the Age of Botnets: Supervised Learning Strategies for Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: New security problems have emerged due to the proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. There is a serious threat to data integrity and network stability from IoT botnets. Maintaining the safety and reliability of IoT ecosystems depends on finding and eliminating botnet attacks on the IoT. An approach to detecting ML-based IoT botnet attacks is the goal of this article. We have constructed and analysed ML models that can identify harmful botnet activity using network traffic data collected from IoT devices. It is possible to detect botnets using these models. To begin, the data must be preprocessed to extract useful characteristics from the network flow. Supervised learning techniques like K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Adaptive Gradient Boosting (AdaBoost), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) are then used to train the model. It is possible to evaluate each model’s performance using measures like F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision. The results of the trials show that ML is a useful tool for detecting botnet assaults on the Internet of Things. Moreover, these results illuminate the possibility of computerised detection techniques to strengthen the IoT’s security and aid in the battle against emerging dangers. In terms of accuracy, the findings show that the KNN model gets 75.42%, the SVM model gets 90.45%, and the AdaBoost model gets 96.21%.
