The model consistently displays an average of roughly 95.25% for precision, recall, or F1-Score metrics across all scales, demonstrating its great accuracy in identifying cases. Support values show that instances are distributed evenly throughout the scales, demonstrating the model's capacity to handle a variety of datasets with effectiveness. Furthermore, the model attains a 99% overall accuracy rate, demonstrating its effectiveness in classifying cases. On a dataset of 14,120 photos, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 85.48 percent. Excellent interpretations are also supported by macro, weighted, and micro average measures of 95.25 percent. In the weighted average, the scores for each class are weighted by its support to counteract class imbalance, while scores for each class are taken into account to give larger classes more importance in the macro average. Micro average, meanwhile, combines all class contributions into a single metric, offering a comprehensive evaluation of the model's effectiveness. Together, these results illustrate how easily the model can spot and categorize examples of different intensities of the same condition. With these consistent results and proven accuracy, a model is a reliable bet for any work that demands precise classification and discrimination. Its potential applications range across a wide variety of fields.

articleTitle: Improved Reinforcement Learning Model for Traffic Management
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This study aims to develop an innovative method to generate a traffic control system on the basis of reinforcement learning. Afterward, its performance is computed concerning WT (waiting time) and SD (Standard Deviation). The results exhibited that the developed method is more effective and superior to traditional methods and leads to mitigate WT and SD. Lower WT indicates that the developed method is effective to manage traffic flow, due to which the congestion is alleviated and enhanced traveling experience is obtained. Additionally, the least SD results in illustrating a more expectable traffic pattern, which makes the travel times more secure and reliable. These findings are useful to enhance metropolitan flexibility and lessen the ecological impact of traffic jamming. The Reinforcement Learning (RL) assists the urban areas in deploying more sustainable transportation schemes, that are helpful for commuters and the setting.

articleTitle: Intelligent Medication Management System: Enhancing Patient-Centric Care with Machine Learning and IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have revolutionized the healthcare industry, particularly in the field of medication administration. The system leverages machine learning algorithms for personalized medical scheduling and Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity for remote monitoring and intervention. Through continuous monitoring and analysis of patient-specific parameters, such as vital signs, medication history, and lifestyle factors, the system dynamically adjusts medication schedules and dosages to optimize therapeutic efficacy while minimizing adverse effects. Key components include a medication dispenser equipped with sensors for inventory tracking and patient interaction detection, a Raspberry Pi microcontroller for data processing, and cloud-based machine learning models for personalized scheduling. Machine learning models are trained on patient-specific data to generate personalized medication schedules considering dosage requirements, timing preferences, and potential interactions. Additionally, the integration of IoT-enabled smart sensors and connectivity allows for smooth communication between patients, healthcare professionals, and medicine dispensers, permitting prompt interventions, prescription reminders, and remote monitoring. Integrated with IoT devices, such as Raspberry Pi-based sensors and actuators, the system enables seamless communication between patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers, facilitating remote monitoring, medication adherence reminders, and timely interventions. Overall, ML and IoT-driven medication dispensing systems offer promising avenues for enhancing medication adherence, reducing errors, and improving patient outcomes in healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: An Energy Interface Circuit for Piezoelectric Using 180nm CMOS Process Technology for Sensor Node Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Piezoelectric energy harvesting has emerged as a promising technology for powering low-power electronic devices by converting ambient mechanical vibrations into electrical energy. However, the efficiency of piezoelectric energy harvesters is often limited due to the variability of the output voltage and current with changes in vibration level and frequency, as well as the generally low output voltage of piezoelectric transducers. This study presents a piezoelectric energy harvester designed to extract energy from the transducer under these condition. The design incorporates synchronized switch harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) technique to effectively manage the variable output of the piezoelectric transducer, a rectifier circuit responsible for converting the AC output of the piezoelectric transducer to DC, and a DC-DC buck converter to step down the rectified DC voltage to the appropriate level for the sensor node load. This advancement in piezoelectric energy harvester design has the potential to provide a reliable power source for sensor nodes application.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Object Identification Techniques for Bird Species
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: While ornithologists fight to maintain biodiversity, nature enthusiasts and environmentalists are also concerned about the well-being of wildlife populations. The share of these lovers has expanded dramatically in recent times, and with a big number of unique animals and birds risking extinction, there are limited options to obtain a single uncommon species. Identifying birds and enjoying bird watching are two completely different challenges. Although public online catalogues exist to identify these birds and to identify objects well identified by machine learning, the methodologies are still uncertain. Therefore, we offer an approach that uses object detection methods such as YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 to conquer this problem. This dataset was built utilizing videos of various birds collected in tropics and sanctuaries for birds. Both approaches were also tested on datasets of varying sizes to offer a full comparison of both approaches and better understand how they function as the dataset and class size rises. To improve the bird detection of our model, this research compares and integrates these two strategies. This hypothesis was that YOLOv8 will deliver improved accuracy than YOLOv5 because it is an upgraded version of the prior model.

articleTitle: Smart IoT Based Real Time Crop Monitoring and Spectrum Management for Hydroponic System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Numerous challenges arise in India, a developing nation heavily reliant on agriculture. These include issues such as small land plots, overuse of pesticides, and substitution of natural nutrients with harmful chemicals. Vertical farming (VF) effectively produces food sustainably while conserving space, natural resources, and labor. This system can be implemented year-round without being affected by seasonal changes, making it adaptable to any location and time. Soil erosion and infertility pose significant challenges in traditional farming. To combat this problem, soilless farming, also called hydroponics, is gaining popularity. Hydroponics is cultivating plants without soil, providing essential nutrients to the crops in a controlled environment. The utilization of research in the VF system for fresh, high-quality, locally-grown produce has risen in the past few years. This approach has been shown to significantly boost productivity and enhance production quality. Vertical farming with hydroponics addresses the issue of limited agricultural land by utilizing vertical space, while hydroponic techniques facilitate organic cultivation. The proposed vertical farming using hydroponics aims to utilize the Internet of Things (IoT) to sense and monitor vital factors like pH, TDS, temperature, and humidity to automate the system.

articleTitle: Environmental Impact Analysis using Satellite Image Processing: A Case Study on Bangalore STRR Phase-1
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Our study plans to conduct a thorough before-and-after analysis of land use and land cover (LULC) alterations in the area surrounding the construction of the Satellite Town Ring Road (STRR) Phase-1, focusing on the environmental implications associated with ongoing highway construction. The STRR Phase-1 will be the focal point for our investigation, allowing us to gain insights into the transformation of the landscape. Our primary objective is to identify the significant changes that have transpired in the area since the initiation of construction activities. Through a comprehensive examination, we aim to gather the impacts on LULC patterns, emphasizing the need for sustainable development practices. The study aspires to contribute valuable information that can guide future development endeavors in a manner that is environmentally responsible. By delving into the intricate dynamics of land use alterations, we seek to inform urban planners, policymakers, and stakeholders about the broader implications of highway construction on the environment. This research aligns with the goal of promoting sustainable urban development and underscores the importance of considering environmental factors in the planning and execution of infrastructure projects.

Author Keywords: satellite image processing,Satellite Town Ring Road (STRR)

articleTitle: Deep CNN with MLP for High Impedance Fault Classification in Power Grids with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Power demand is increasing day by day for continuing the industries, commercial loads, and household loads due to the increasing population, and it requires consistent power to sustain life. Integrating renewable energy sources into the grid is increasing tremendously to meet the power demand. The fault is one barrier in the power system that interrupts the smooth growing country. High impedance fault (HIF) classification is the main challenge in power system distribution networks due to the low magnitude of fault current. In addition to having low current, HIFs have other typical properties comparable to the characteristics of switching events, like load switching, such as unpredictability, nonlinearity, etc. Adding distributed generators (DGs) to the distribution system modifies the substation’s current contribution and impacts HIF detection. In this paper, fault classification has been done, including HIF using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). A distribution network integrated with different distributed generators like solar PV panels, Doubly fed induction generators (DFIG), and Diesel generators. Various possible configurations with different inception angles, fault distances, types of faults, and HIF are created in data generation. The weighted average accuracy for fault classification is 99.46% achieved through 10-fold cross-validation of the proposed Deep CNN with MLP model. Various comparisons have been made in the discussion section of the proposed model with existing deep learning models.

articleTitle: Securing Digital Evidence In Forensic Investigation Using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Throughout the technological age of today, data plays a major role in every work period. As data is subject to change, it should be secure. We'll talk about data capacity and portrayal in diverse organizations. Attacks against information that is vital to a particular association are possible. Evidence gathered from crime scenes is crucial to wrapping up the investigation and giving the parties justice. Therefore, it's crucial to keep these proofs safe from any type of tampering. Given that digitalization of forensic evidence management systems is an environmentally friendly paradigm, it is imperative. Blockchains are distributed ledgers of transactions that are digitally distributed, cryptographically signed, and arranged chronologically into blocks. They are fully accessible to all members of the blockchain network. As cybercrime increases quickly, attackers act malevolently to change those data. However, it is significantly affecting forensic evidence, which is necessary for provenance. Result, it is necessary to preserve the validity and provenance of digital evidence as it moves through the several phases of forensic inquiry. We've tested and implemented dApps in a local blockchain environment by using Ganache, an Ethereum development tool. Our development process has benefited greatly from Ganache's deterministic behaviour, account management capabilities, gas control, and connection with frameworks such as Truffle involves a forensic chain where the produced report travels via a number of stages or middlemen, including a pathology lab, a physician, a police agency, etc. Blockchain technology is better appropriate for creating a transparent system with immutable forensic evidence.

articleTitle: Inception and LightGBM-based Model for Poly-Cystic Ovary Syndrome Detection with CNN in Ultra-sound Images
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Nowadays, a common hormonal condition that affects women of reproductive age and frequently results in infertility is Poly-Cystic ovary syndrome. Recognizing the Poly-Cystic ovary syndrome early is essential for symptom management and mitigating associated health risks. The traditional methods are used for diagnosis, encompassing high androgen levels, anovulation, and Poly-Cystic ovaries observed via ultra-sound. However, the challenging aspect of manually assessing Poly-Cystic ovaries observed via ultra-sound through follicle counting and thickness determination by medical professionals persists. In addition to addressing patient symptoms, clinicians must rely on a combination of biochemical and clinical indicators, lacking standardized diagnostic procedures. To alleviate these diagnostic challenges, this paper presents a hybrid Poly-Cystic Ovary Syndrome Detection model using a convolutional neural network comprising an ensemble inception model and a light gradient-boosting machine on ultra-sound Images. It significantly improves the detection of the Poly-Cystic ovaries observed and achieves an accuracy of 98.4%, surpassing InceptionV3’s 96.3%. This study substantiates this performance gain through comprehensive quantitative effectiveness assessment metrics. This study proposes a promising model for accurate and efficient Poly-Cystic ovary syndrome diagnosis, aiding clinicians in providing timely and targeted care to affected individuals.

articleTitle: Detecting Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Alzheimer’s is a neurological condition that worsens over time and affects cognitive and memory abilities. Because AD is so common, prompt intervention and therapy depend on early detection. Conventional diagnostic techniques, such neuroimaging and clinical evaluations, frequently have poor specificity and sensitivity, which can result in delayed or incorrect diagnoses. This paper investigates the use of ML techniques for the fast detection of AD. Using a longitudinal dataset of 150 people having age ranging from 60 to 96, this study examines seven ML algorithms named Support Vector Machine (SVM), Voting Classifier, Decision Tree , Gradient Booster, Random Forest Classifier, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and the MLP i.e. Multi layer perceptron—to assess their efficacy in identifying AD. Biomarkers such as the Normalized Whole Brain Volume, Clinical Dementia Rating i.e. CDR and Mini-Mental State Examination i.e. MMSE are included in the dataset. The results show that MLP has the lowest accuracy at 56.25%, while Random Forest and Gradient Boosting classifiers obtain the best accuracy of roughly 83.92%. This comparison investigation shows that AD detection can become more precised with the machine learning algorithms. Additionally, this work implies that future detection systems might benefit from increased accuracy through the integration of various models and the combination of textual and image data. These revelations support continued efforts to create effective and trustworthy Alzheimer’s disease diagnostic instruments.

articleTitle: Automated Teller Machine (ATM) Ethernet Traffic Analysis for Enhanced Forensic Detection of IP Packets
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Over the past few decades, consumers have become increasingly reliant on the convenience of Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) for a variety of banking needs, including transferring funds between accounts, checking account balances, and withdrawing cash from savings, checking, and other account types. This convenience has been further enhanced by mobile banking apps, which allow users to easily locate nearby ATMs. Nevertheless, these advantages have been accompanied by a sharp increase in ATM fraud globally, which has negatively affected consumer trust in banks, credit card companies, and ATMs. The perceived level of security in ATM transactions and the technology that supports these transactions is crucial to maintaining trust. Tackling the risks associated with ATM fraud and reducing its impact is a pressing issue for financial institutions, particularly as fraud techniques have become more advanced and sophisticated. Historically, the verification process for ATM transactions utilized the Plain Old Telephone Service (POTS). However, there has been a shift towards using Ethernet connections to link ATMs with processors, banks, and card issuers. This transition has increased both the size and complexity of the attack surface, presenting new security challenges. Given these heightened security risks, it is imperative for the industry to thoroughly investigate all potential attack surfaces. This research focuses specifically on the Ethernet packets that facilitate these transactions. By examining the structure and predictability of ATM Ethernet traffic, this study aims to provide insights that can help in developing more robust forensic detection methods. Despite the proliferation of retail ATMs in everyday locations, such as shopping centers and convenience stores, this particular attack vector has received relatively little attention in the field of cybersecurity. In this research, we delve into the intricacies of ATM Ethernet traffic, analyzing packet structures to identify patterns and potential vulnerabilities. The goal is to enhance the understanding of this often-overlooked attack vector and to propose strategies for mitigating risks associated with Ethernet-based transactions. By doing so, this research aims to contribute to the development of more effective security measures that can protect both consumers and financial institutions from the evolving threat of ATM fraud. Through a detailed exploration of Ethernet traffic in ATM operations, this study seeks to support the creation of more secure and reliable banking environments, ultimately restoring and maintaining consumer confidence in the safety of ATM transactions.

articleTitle: Dimensional Hidden Layers and their Impact on Neural Network Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Increasing the dimensionality of the ANN model architecture from 1D to 2D, 3D and Investigating the impact of a novel approach on this ANN model by replacing the neuron in a hidden layer with another hidden layer containing a neuron. 1D contains 3 hidden layers with 64 neurons each,2D also contains 3 main-hidden layers but each hidden layer contains 2 more sub-hidden layers inside with 32 neurons, similarly in 3D there are 3 main-hidden layers inside each there are 2 more sub-hidden layers inside those hidden layers there are 2 more inner hidden layers containing 16 neurons. One of the approach is with making an dense connection and the other is to go sequential 2D model has performed 10% better than the 1D whereas the 3d model has an better performance of 11-12% in an dense connection, In sequential 2D model has performed 15% better than the 1D whereas the 3d model achieved an accuracy similarly to that of the 1D model but the visualization show's that the model has used only few neuron to give the same results. This help in explore more complex relationships and achieve competitive accuracy despite higher model complexity. All models are trained under identical conditions, highlighting the potential of increased dimensionality to optimize model performance efficiently.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling for Concrete Compressive Strength: ML-Regressors, Custom Neural Networks, and Explainable AI Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Concrete compressive strength is crucial for optimizing concrete mix designs in construction. This study employs traditional machine learning regressors, custom ANNs, and Explainable AI (XAI) techniques using a dataset from Kaggle with 1030 instances and 9 attributes. Among the models tested, Random Forest Regression exhibited the best performance with the lowest MSE and highest R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) values. Custom ANNs, particularly a five-layer architecture with SeLU and ReLU activations optimized using the Adam optimizer, achieved superior results with an MSE of 22.2 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.92. To ensure model transparency, we used the LIME technique, revealing the contributions of individual input variables. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of advanced ML models and XAI techniques in predicting concrete compressive strength, offering a robust framework for optimizing concrete mix designs and enhancing construction practices. Future research can expand on these results by exploring larger datasets, additional features, and more advanced XAI methods.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Customer Segmentation: A Fusion of Clustering Algorithm and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Customer segmentation is a vital part of modern business strategy, where the goal is to organize the different types of customers a business has. This helps in understanding their unique characteristics and behaviors. The tricky part is dealing with the massive amount of data and finding meaningful patterns to improve marketing and operations. When done right, customer segmentation can supercharge a business. It lets companies tailor their marketing to fit specific customer groups, use resources wisely, and ultimately make customers happier.Traditional clustering algorithms have been widely used for this purpose, but recent advancements in machine learning, particularly neural networks, offer promising opportunities for more accurate and efficient segmentation. This paper explores the fusion of clustering algorithms, including agglomerative hierarchical clustering, K-means clustering, and affinity propagation, with neural networks to revolutionize customer segmentation. Through a comprehensive review of literature and empirical analysis, we demonstrate the potential of this approach in enhancing segmentation accuracy, scalability, and interpretability.The beauty of this approach is that it can work with real-time data. In the fast-changing world of customer behavior, this is a big deal. It gives businesses an edge, allowing them to adjust their strategies quickly as customer preferences change. In the end, it’s not just about accurate segmentation; it’s about helping businesses grow and serve customers better.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence driven Deep Learning for Competitive Intelligence to enhance Market Analysis and Strategic Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This research provides insight into the successful application of modern deep learning techniques such as Transfer Learning, BERT, and Autoencoders to develop a powerful tool to sustain market analysis and strategic positioning in competitive intelligence. The conducted analysis proved that BERT was the most effective technique, as it produced the highest results in regards of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score values in all ten trials. The results of the experiment showed that with accuracy ranging from 90.5% to 92.3%, precision from 91.2% to 93.0%, recall from 89.7% to 91.7%, and F1 score from 90.4% to 92.2%, BERT proved to be the best technique for extracting insights from various textual data sources. In and of itself, Transfer Learning also yielded promising results, and its accuracy ranged from 85.2% to 88.6%, precision from 86.5% to 89.9%, recall from 83.7% to 87.3%, and F1 score from 85.0% to 88.5%. Additionally, given its ability to adapt to particular tasks with quite limited labeled data, Transfer Learning is a valuable tool for market analysis. In this experiment for Autoencoders, it has been shown that they provided a slightly lower performance than BERT and Transfer Learning. The reconstruction error of the deep learning method used in this experiment ranged from 0.018 to 0.025, while accuracy varied from 87.9% to 90.3%. Nevertheless, further optimization can make autoencoders a promising approach for market analysis. Thus, this research indicates the vital importance of leveraging advanced deep learning techniques for gaining a competitive advantage in the present-day business environment.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Potential of Combined CNN-RF Fusion Strategies for Accurate Fabric Flaw Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In the abstract, Fabric defect identification is critical for ensuring the high standards and authenticity of fabrics in the manufacturing sector. This article describes and analyses a novel technique for fabric defect detection that combines neural networks using convolution (CNNs) with a Random Forest (RF) classifier. The investigation includes a broad dataset of fabric photos with labelled defect labels that span a wide range of defect types, like skewing, pilling, barre, triple pick/double conclusion, grease stains, knots, wrinkles, among fading. The method is evaluated by doing a thorough analysis of the accuracy, recollection, and F1-score metrics for each defect class. Precision scores range from 94.84% can 95.58%, illustrating the system's ability to accurately acknowledge positive events while minimising the number of false positives. At the same time, recall rates that range from 94.88% to 95.58% illustrate the model's ability to detect actual positive events while minimizing false negatives. The first-place scores, which integrate memory and accuracy, are consistent across all faulty courses, ranging at 95.19%. The support values, which represent the total number of occurrences for each category, provide information on the dataset's distribution, improving the model's capacity for generalization effectively. In addition, macro weighted, but microscopic average measurements reveal The simulation's balanced but effective performance in detecting defects in fabric. The suggested method yields a total accuracy of 99%, proving its capacity for accurately identifying imperfections in fabric. The investigation described here contributes to the creation of computerized quality assurance methods in the textile industry by presenting an accurate and effective method for identifying fabric flaws.

articleTitle: A Digital Dermoscopy: CNNs in the Era of Automated Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: A crucial job in dermatology is the detection of skin cancer, which requires accurate classification between benign and malignant lesions. To automate the categorization of skin cancer, this research looks into the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), with a particular emphasis on differentiating between benign and malignant lesions. To improve model resilience and generalization, a large dataset were carefully selected of dermatoscopic pictures from reliable medical sources. We then used methods including scaling, normalization, and augmentation. We simultaneously tracked training and validation metrics during iterative training across many epochs. The model's increasing prediction accuracy is shown by our findings, which show a steady decrease in training and validation loss across epochs. Accuracy grows gradually at the same time, demonstrating CNNs' efficacy in correctly diagnosing skin lesions. Its remarkable accuracy of 0.98 after 50 epochs demonstrates the model's potential. Further support of the model's stability is provided by validation measurements, which show that validation accuracy peaked at 0.83 across many epochs. These results highlight CNNs' potential as formidable instruments for automated skin cancer diagnosis, offering improved accuracy and effectiveness in clinical contexts. Subsequent investigations need to concentrate on enhancing and perfecting CNN-based techniques for realistic use in the identification and categorization of skin cancer.

articleTitle: Combining KNN Algorithm with Traditional DGA Techniques for Transformer Defect Identification and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This paper explores the application of KNN for identifying and analyzing dissolved gases in power transformer (PT) oil. We want to make a strong diagnostic model that can correctly classify different kinds of PT defects by combining traditional dissolved gas analysis (DGA) methods with the KNN algorithm. To do this, traditional techniques like Doernenburg ratio techniques (DRT), International Electrotechnical Commission ratio techniques (IECRT), and Duval triangle techniques (DTT) are used to prepare the DGA data. These ratios are then used as input features for the KNN model. The main objective of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of the KNN-based model in diagnosing PT defects and to compare its performance with traditional techniques. Key metrics such as accuracy, F1 score, specificity, precision, and recall will be used to evaluate the model’s effectiveness. Furthermore, the study will explore the impact of different input features on model performance to identify the optimal feature set for accurate defect diagnosis.

articleTitle: Automated Multilingual Validation for HMI Using Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The growing demand for multilingual Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI) in ovens presents challenges in ensuring precision across various languages. This study introduces a solution using image processing and machine learning (ML) to automate language testing for HMI, enhancing robustness and accuracy. By utilizing Pattern Match and ML techniques, we validate text from HMI screens in multiple languages, improving efficiency, reducing human error, and speeding up multilingual HMI deployment. Automating this process for 26 languages has reduced manual effort and testing time by 87.%, successfully validating over 32,000 strings. Key components include data collection, model training, and system integration, resulting in increased customer satisfaction, shorter development cycles, and improved market competitiveness. This technology ensures scalability, better resource allocation, and consistent quality across different languages.

Author Keywords: Human Machine Interface and Image Processing

articleTitle: Text to Video Generation using Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Press Reports in general have been published in text based format for a vast period of time, although the old way of publishing reports may have been effective initially, it has led to a decrease in audience engagement and attention span. The study offers a novel solution to the problem of users’ attention spans getting shorter. Therefore, to retain user engagement and increase content quality, the proposed solution aims to create an automated system that uses press reports to generate dynamic video content. This technology improves user comprehension and engagement by utilizing audio-visual synthesis and natural language processing techniques. The models that are implemented have performed well during the Testing Phase by showing an average accuracy of 82 percentage from the NLP Large Language Models and 89 percentage from the Machine Learning Models and the outcomes reveal increased knowledge retention and user engagement. Finally, this study offers a novel method of communication by automatically converting press releases into videos for maximum viewer engagement.

articleTitle: Efficient Waste Services in High-rise Buildings Leveraging LSTM Time Series Forecasting and IoT Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The preservation of natural resources in the environment depends on effective waste management in high-rise buildings. Enhancing waste services in such buildings is the focus of this research, which presents a groundbreaking technique that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) automation with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) time series forecasting. By analyzing data on trash creation in the past, the LSTM model can accurately forecast how much garbage will be generated in the future. IoT sensors are embedded in waste cans to track when they are full and send that information to an advanced management system. This system seamlessly combines LSTM forecasting with IoT automation to provide real-time garbage collection schedule adjustments that are influenced by both present and expected demand. Waste management operating costs and energy usage may be significantly reduced with this proactive strategy, which optimizes collection routes and avoids wasteful collections. The system ensures effective resource usage and allows for prompt interventions with real-time monitoring and alarms enabled by IoT technology. Traditional waste collection systems may not be feasible or efficient in high-rise buildings, which present their own set of problems compared to the suggested solution. The system provides a sustainable and cost-effective waste management approach that is customized to the unique demands of high-rise settings via the integration of advanced forecasting algorithms and IoT automation. This technique improves the quality of life for people while contributing to the sustainability objectives of urban development.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Model that can Generate Abstractive Summaries for Multimedia Content such as Videos, Audio and Text to Provide Concise and Informative Descriptions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Multimedia data, comprising text, audio, and video, has become increasingly prevalent in today's digital landscape, leading to a growing need for effective summarization techniques. In an era inundated with multimedia data, spanning text, audio, and video, the task of generating coherent and concise summaries has assumed paramount importance. Deep Learning (DL) techniques have emerged as powerful tools for tackling the multifaceted challenges posed by multimedia summarization. This research focuses on summarization methods that harness the power of Deep Learning (DL) to extract meaningful content from diverse multimedia formats. The objective is to provide a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art DL techniques employed in summarizing multimedia data. By exploring various multimedia formats and their associated challenges, this study contributes to the evolving landscape of multimedia summarization, offering insights into its applications and future potential. Overall, this study aims to deepen our understanding of DL-based multimedia summarization techniques and their implications in the context of an increasingly data-rich digital world.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Framework for Effective Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This Study presents a novel method for identifying anomalies in time series datasets by employing deep learning algorithms. Our approach blends autoencoders with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Although we concentrate our experiments on data related to electric vehicles (EVs), our overall objective is to show how flexible our method is for detecting anomalies in a variety of time-based datasets. The Autoencoder's capacity to rebuild input sequences and identify anomalies based on reconstruction mistakes is complementary to the LSTM network's ability to capture complex temporal patterns. By combining these methods, we provide a strong structure that may be employed to determine abnormalities in time series data and support well-informed decision-making in a variety of contexts. The accurate detection of abnormalities by our method improves the dependability of data analysis. Subsequent investigations may investigate additional improvements and expansions of LSTM and Autoencoder models with the goal of finding outliers in time series data.

articleTitle: Insightful Tuberculosis Detection: Integrating CNNs with Explainable LIME Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: One of the most transmissible illnesses and one of the top 10 causes of mortality globally is tuberculosis (TB). The effective treatment and control of tuberculosis (TB), which still poses a major danger to global health, depends on an early and accurate diagnosis. Although the manual interpretation of chest X-ray (CXR) imaging is laborious and prone to error, it is essential for the diagnosis of tuberculosis (TB). This work uses current breakthroughs in deep learning to build an automated method for TB detection from CXR photos. After collecting and preprocessing a range of annotated CXR picture datasets, convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures are investigated for model generation. Pre-trained models are refined on the dataset using transfer learning approaches, which are also included to improve diversity and reduce class disparity. Conventional metrics are utilized to evaluate the trained model on an unbiased test set by comparison to baseline methods and expert radiologist interpretations.

articleTitle: Advanced Sunflower Leaf Disease Detection Using CNN-SVM Hybrid Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: An extensive investigation of effectiveness metrics derived from a classification system intended to identify several common disorders in sunflower leaves is presented in the abstract. The model's accuracy, recall, or F1-score are important performance metrics that indicate how well it can categorize various illness categories. Outstanding results, which span from 96.65% to 98.75% in all disease categories, demonstrate how robust and dependable the model is at misidentifying both damaged and healthy sunflower leaves. The abstract demonstrates how well the model performs, with a total precision of around 96.75% for a data set comprising 9,695 photos. The model's overall effectiveness and the degree to which it correctly recalls every positive instance and recognizes positive occurrences are both shown through the F1-score, which corresponds to the harmonic average of these two measures. Every type of sickness in the dataset has support values according to the number of instances in each category. The representative dataset was trained to remove all preexisting trends, and class distribution also plays a major factor in mitigating bias in learning new concepts. Deep learning model level d at the staying different illness, just various levels of nourishment health, or types of medicines than fighter planes, support rates of these diseases will make it a delightful close whistle and the quotient. As a disease management tool in sunflower farming, the classification model showed an overall precision of 99% in identifying illnesses like blight, with high accuracy. Timely, focused action has armed farmers to help prevent diseases and keep crops free from disease now. The model's excellent performance metrics in this evaluation point to its effectiveness at diagnosing infections; they're also an opportunity to better understand both agricultural output and sustainable methods for growing sunflowers.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation and Energy Efficient Dynamic Particle Swarm Optimisation in Heterogeneous Wireless Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the difficult of beam policy in a multi-user peer-to-peer web linkage setting as part of our research. Using a network simulator, the dynamic particle swarm optimization is suggested for this. The challenge is to limit the maximum power consumption per relay, according to minimal Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) guarantees, after a complete Channel State Information (CSI) is established. It has been established that the non-convex problem satisfies a potent duality. The twofold problem with the highest polynomial complexity was given as Semi Definite Programming (SDP). On the basis of the standards of the optimal dual variables, we looked at the best beam forming vectors for the initial problems in 3 different scenarios. This demonstrated whether the minimum Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) prerequisite for each S-D pair has been met as well as whether a relay's electricity consumption varies among relays.

articleTitle: Nutrition Monitoring based on Food Image Classification Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Image classification, which teaches computers to understand and categorize visual input, is a crucial challenge in computer vision technology. Applications for this job are numerous and include autonomous vehicle navigation, medical image analysis, and object recognition in photos. These labels can represent various objects, scenes, or patterns present in the images. We have selected the topic of image classification of Indian food items and hence display their calorie values after assessing all the major classification techniques. In the recent past, most middle and upper class people in India are at that stage where they are becoming health conscious and hence this application will be very useful for the health enthusiasts as they will get the idea of how much calories they are consuming while having food (especially junk food). The rich and diverse culinary landscape of Indian cuisine presents a unique challenge for automated image classification systems. This paper explores the application of deep learning techniques to accurately classify Indian food items based on visual features extracted from images.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Approach to Mitigating Vulnerabilities in the Mobile Operating System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The widespread adoption of the Android operating system in mobile devices has made it an attractive target for cyber attackers. As the Android ecosystem continues to grow, the need for robust prevention and detection mechanisms to safeguard against potential vulnerabilities becomes increasingly paramount. In this research paper, we present a comprehensive approach to address the critical issue of vulnerability exploitation in Android platform. The study commences with an in-depth analysis of the Android platform using the Metasploit framework, simulating real-world attack scenarios to identify potential weak points. By exposing these vulnerabilities, the work gains valuable insights into the techniques employed by malicious actors to exploit Android platform weaknesses. Subsequently, this project delves into the development of an effective prevention strategy to fortify the Android platform against potential threats. The proposed technique provides a multi-layered defense mechanism, encompassing secure coding practices, permission management, and enhanced access controls, aimed at bolstering the overall resilience of the system. The work demonstrates this process by exploiting the Android platform using a malicious script created via msfvenom, log captures while executing script and analysis gives a decision about genuine or malicious application using LOG ANALYSIS script. This work also aims to prevent malicious code activities in Android platform by using proposed security rules.

articleTitle: A Convolution Neural Network Based Classifier for Discerning AI Generated Images and Real Images
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The exponential advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has led to the creation of synthetic images that closely resemble real-world photographs. However, the widespread distribution of AI-generated content poses significant challenges in distinguishing between genuine and synthetic imagery, particularly in cybersecurity, content moderation, and image forensics. Traditional image classification methods struggle with this task due to the striking visual similarities between the two types of images. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have emerged as powerful tools for image classification, leveraging their ability to extract complex features from raw pixel data. In this study, we propose an enhanced CNN methodology to differentiate between AI-generated and real images. Specifically, we focus on three popular CNN architectures: ResNet-50, RexNet-150, and RexNet-200. By augmenting these models with advanced architectural enhancements and training strategies, we aim to improve their discriminative capabilities. Our experimental findings reveal that RexNet-150 surpasses ResNet-50 and RexNet-200, achieving superior accuracy in distinguishing between AI-generated and real images. RexNet-150 attained an impressive 97.9% accuracy on the test dataset, outperforming ResNet-50 (93.1%) and RexNet-200 (90.3%). Moreover, RexNet-150 demonstrated enhanced training convergence and speed, indicating its effectiveness in learning discriminative features for image classification tasks. The superior performance of RexNet-150 holds significant implications for online safety, content moderation, and image authenticity detection. These advancements in CNN technology foster trust in digital imagery and enhance confidence in AI applications across diverse domains.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable UI /UX Design for Robotic Applications based on User Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In this research, we present a novel method aimed at enhancing the user experience (UX) in robotic applications through a customizable UI/UX system that adapts to users' skill levels. The Continuous Testing and Optimization method ensures that the system dynamically adjusts its graphical user interface (GUI) in response to users' evolving proficiency levels in C++ programming. The primary objective of the adaptive UI/UX system is to optimize usability and user satisfaction through iterative refinement guided by qualitative feedback analysis, and user performance metrics. This approach enables the system to cater to users with varying levels of expertise, offering personalized learning pathways for novice, intermediate, and advanced users. The seamless integration of the adaptive GUI for an Educational Programming Robot within the system architecture further enhances the individualized learning experience for users. To validate the effectiveness of the system, two studies were conducted. These studies demonstrate the system's ability to accurately measure user expertise and dynamically adjust the GUI based on users' proficiency levels. The results of these studies indicate significant improvements in user experience and learning outcomes. This underscores the potential of reconfigurable UI/UX design to promote personalized skill development within robotic applications. By leveraging continuous testing and optimization, our approach addresses the challenge of adapting interfaces to users' changing needs and proficiency levels, paving the way for more effective human-robot interaction and skill acquisition.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Lidar in a Self Driving Wheelchair
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Wheel-chair robotics has emerged as a promising technology with notable advancements over the years promoting mobility and enhancing the lives of people who are physically challenged. Autonomous navigation has paved the way in implementing self-driving wheelchairs with the help of lidar sensor, camera, and other different technical devices. Through our study, we conducted a thorough analysis by comparing and visualizing three distinct 2D LiDAR placement positions on a wheelchair robot called Self-E, following autonomous navigation in three different environments. By testing the self-driving wheelchair robot in diverse environments, we aimed to assess its adaptability and effectiveness across different real-world scenarios. We meticulously recorded key factors such as navigation time, collision occurrences, area coverage, and map accuracy. The robot's trajectory and environmental perception are recorded for each Lidar position. The simulations are performed using gazebo platform and the obtained maps were visualized using Rviz in Robotic Operating System (ROS ecosystem). This research provides valuable insights into optimizing LiDAR sensor placement to enhance the performance of wheelchair robots in real-world environments.

articleTitle: Corrosion Image Classification using Deep Learning and Transfer Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Corrosion, a pervasive challenge across numerous industries, undermines material integrity and incurs substantial economic costs. Traditional methods of corrosion detection are often labour-intensive and prone to human error. Innovative solutions for timely and accurate identification are needed. This study explores applying Deep Learning (DL) and Transfer Learning (TL) techniques for classifying corrosion images into five distinct classes. This work uses the Worcester Polytechnic Institute's dataset, which consists of 600 corrosion image samples expertly rated according to the ASTM D1654 standard. This dataset is used to develop and compare the performance of custom Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with TL approaches using VGG16 and ResNet50 models. The results indicate that TL models significantly outperform the custom CNN in training and validation accuracy, with VGG16 achieving the highest validation accuracy of 90% after fine-tuning. This work highlights the efficacy of leveraging pre-trained models and fine-tuning them for specific tasks. The results lay the groundwork for developing robust and generalized models capable of excelling in diverse real-world scenarios, enhancing maintenance strategies, improving safety, and significantly reducing costs across various industries.

articleTitle: Optimizing Lender Portfolios: A P2P Lending Recommendation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The proliferation of peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platforms has ushered in a new era of financial accessibility, but it has also brought to the forefront the growing concern of loan defaults. This paper explores the increasing significance of P2P lending platforms and addresses the critical issue of loan default prediction. The study focuses on the application of machine learning techniques, specifically employing the Random Forest algorithm and logistic regression, to train a predictive model for assessing the likelihood of default within a loan portfolio. The primary objective is to enhance the decision-making process for lenders by recommending optimal loan portfolios based on the predictive insights generated by the model. By leveraging the capabilities of this robust algorithm, the research aims to contribute to the advancement of risk assessment methodologies in P2P lending, ultimately fostering more informed and secure lending practices on these platforms. We trained and compared logistic Reression and random forest models and derived resultant optimal portfolio by considering both the models which is intended to give better results than a single model.

articleTitle: Empowering Early Detection: CervicalCareXG Revolutionizes Cervical type cancer Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: A XGBoost-Based System in Cervical type cancer Diagnostics are proposed in the current research work. Generally Cervical type of cancer will be a significant health concern worldwide, particularly in the regions with limited access on advanced healthcare facilities. On Early detection will plays a pivotal role on improving patient outcomes and by reducing mortality rates. In this study, the propose system termed CervicalCareXG, a novelistic system for cervical type cancer diagnostics depends on the XGBoost methodology. CervicalCareXG will utilizes a machine Learning-Driven approach to analyze patient data, also including demographic information, medical history, and cervical screening results, to Prediction the likelihood of cervical type cancer development. The XGBoost algorithm, known for its prediction accuracy and efficacy in handling complex health related datasets, is employed to train a predictive model with a capable of identifying high-risk individuals who may requires further diagnostic evaluation or preventive interventions. Through comprehensively evaluation using reality patient data, CervicalCareXG may demonstrates a promising performance in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receivers operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC). Thus, it showcases its potential as a valuable tool for healthcare professionals on cervical type cancer screening programs. By harnessing the power of machine Learning-Driven and XGBoost, CervicalCareXG with an aim to contribute to the early detection and management of cervical type cancer, ultimately by improving patient outcomes and reducing the burden of this devastating disease.

articleTitle: Enhancing Web Security through Machine Learning: A Random Forest Approach to Malicious URL Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Detecting malicious URLs by employing the Random Forest algorithm alongside URL parsing techniques. The dataset comprises URLs categorized into phishing, benign, and defacement classes. By parsing these URLs, various features are extracted, such as domain name, abnormality indicators, security status, URL shortening presence, and IP address presence. These features are utilized to train the Random Forest classifier. The Random Forest model learns to differentiate between different URL types based on the extracted features. A feature importance analysis is conducted to identify the most influential features affecting classification decisions. The effectiveness of the approach is evaluated by assessing the accuracy of the Random Forest classifier on training, testing, and out-of-bag (OOB) data. The model's ability to accurately classify URLs aids in identifying potential security threats, including phishing attacks, website defacement, and other online risks. By automating the detection of malicious URLs, the model contributes to enhancing web security measures. This model presents a comprehensive methodology for detecting malicious URLs through the integration of machine learning and URL-parsing techniques. The evaluation of the Random Forest classifier's accuracy on multiple datasets demonstrates its effectiveness in proactively identifying and addressing security vulnerabilities in online environments. This approach provides organizations with a valuable tool for bolstering online security and mitigating cyber threats.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in HRM: Transforming Employee Retention through Predictive Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Employee turnover is one of the central facets of personnel management that can affect organizational performance significantly. In this study, the author discusses the use of artificial neural networks to point out the possibility of employee turnover and the way to improve the retention rate as well. To address the research questions posed by this investigation, the study acquires and integrates several features that are demographic, job-related, performance-related, and engagement-related data of a large organization. The approach entails data preparation analysis, model creation, and assessment by utilization of a multi-layered pattern neural network. The analysis reveals that the deep learning model achieves superior predictive performance to conventional ML models including logistic regression and decision trees concerning identifying employee turnover. To be precise, for the model based on the structure of a neural network, the efficiency was tested with 91% accuracy, 89% of precision, 86% of recall, and 87% of the F1-score. Importantly, the results presented above demonstrate that the model developed in the current research is highly useful in everyday practice, particularly in terms of accurately identifying employees at risk for turnover to the organization. Such insights into the subject contribute to understanding the ability of deep learning to revolutionize HRM, as it offers more accurate insights into the behavior of employees. Using such enhancements in the course of predictive analytics, HR professionals are capable of enhancing interventions together with proactive retention mechanisms which in turn leads to low rates of turnover costs and foster productivity of qualified workforce. The given research adds to the knowledge in the area of predictive analytics in the context of HRM and paves the way for the development of further research in the field.

articleTitle: Analysis of Classification and Stage-wise Prediction Techniques of Melanoma
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Melanoma prediction is a skin cancer, and one in seventeen people is affected by this disease. Identifying and classifying early stages is an important research area in this field. Different research has been conducted in this field. This disease spreads to every body part, so early prediction and classification are very important for medical diagnosis. This paper presented a brief survey of melanoma prediction, classification and early-stage analysis and predictions. In particular, machine- and deep-learning-based techniques are used to analyze and predict melanoma. In this paper, different dataset details and metrics for evaluation are also presented in the assessment and implementation of models. Finally, the future direction of the research is also given for further study.

articleTitle: Breaking Down Barriers: Next-Generation Techniques for Segmenting Medical Abstract Text using DeBERTa-V3
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The readability of medical research paper abstracts is often compromised by their dense, complex language and format, which consolidates key information into a single, challenging paragraph. This study introduces a novel application of Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to enhance the segmentation and readability of these abstracts, making them more accessible and skimmable for rapid review. Utilizing the advanced capabilities of PyTorch, we developed an NLP model leveraging the pretrained DeBERTa-v3 Base model from HuggingFace to segment medical abstracts into discrete, intelligible units. This approach was inspired by the architecture discussed in the State of the art Techniques(SOTA’s) which provided foundational insights into sentence classification within medical texts. Our model not only segments text but also maintains the logical and semantic continuity essential for understanding medical findings. Preliminary results demonstrate a significant improvement in the readability of segmented abstracts compared to their unsegmented counterparts when compared to Universal Sentence Encode(USE). This paper details the development process, the comparative analysis with USE, and the potential implications of this enhanced readability in medical literature.

articleTitle: Real-Time Train Tracking and Time Prediction System For Railway System in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This research focuses on enhancing Sri Lanka’s railway system through a Real-Time Train Tracking and Time Prediction System, tailored to the country’s unique railway network. The system integrates advanced technologies like machine learning and GPS for precise time predictions, which are communicated via a website. The study begins with an in-depth analysis of Sri Lanka’s existing railway infrastructure and operational complexities. Train NO. 1015, which travels daily from Colombo to Badulla, was selected for this research. Factors such as weather, passenger delays, operational requirements, signaling errors, and staff delays were identified as challenges to accurate time predictions through an extensive data analysis of past train delay data. The system design includes a machine learning algorithm using LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) neural networks for predicting train arrival times, and a user-friendly interface for displaying these predictions. The goal is to provide real-time insights for railway authorities and reliable travel information for passengers through a user-friendly web application.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Rooftop Photovoltaic Panel from Satellite and Aerial Images using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This research paper investigates the application of Deep Learning, specifically employing the DeepLabV3 architecture, for Semantic Segmentation in identifying Rooftop Photovoltaic (PV) Panels from both Satellite and Aerial Images. The primary objective is to compute solar panel efficiency through precise identification and spatial analysis of PV panels. Leveraging DeepLabV3's pixel-level segmentation, this study provides detailed insights that enable a comprehensive assessment of solar panel performance. The proposed methodology involves the utilization of DeepLabV3 on satellite and aerial images, with a focus on classifying pixels corresponding to solar panels and deriving efficiency metrics. The research outcomes aim to enhance solar energy utilization and facilitate informed decision-making in the renewable energy sector. The experimental results indicate that the recognition using DeepLabV3 achieves an accuracy of 75%.

articleTitle: Binary Classification of Lung Diseases Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This study explores the use of a hybrid machine learning model that combines support vector machines (SVMs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for the diagnosis of lung disorders in humans, with a focus on differentiating between healthy and infected lung states. A balanced dataset was used to thoroughly assess the model's performance, and important metrics including precision, recall, F1-score, accuracy, and support were measured. The model obtained an F1-Score of 93.40%, a Precision of 93.17%, and a Recall of 93.63% for the Healthy class. Comparably, the F1-Score was 93.32%, the Precision was 93.55%, and the Recall was 93.08% for the Infected Lung class. A well-balanced assessment was ensured by the fact that each class made up 50% of the sample, with 8010 examples for Healthy and 7950 for Infected Lungs. The model performed well, with a total accuracy of 93%. Additionally, the precision, recall, and F1-score macro, weighted, as well as micro averages were consistently 93.36%, demonstrating consistent efficacy across many assessment criteria. These findings demonstrate the possibility of merging CNNs with SVMs in the analysis of medical images, offering a trustworthy and effective diagnostic tool for the identification of lung diseases. To further enhance and validate the model's performance, the study highlights the significance of advanced machine learning techniques in improving diagnostic accuracy and suggests future research directions, such as dataset expansion, integration of additional imaging modalities, and clinical validation.

articleTitle: Cross-Institutional Breast Tumor Detection via Federated Learning and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Among all cancer diseases, breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death, thus the need for enhanced methods for early identification. This study seeks to determine the applicability of federated learning techniques in detecting breast tumors using a CNN among five clients. Every individual, each client, works on a model that can be shared while at the same time ensuring that data cannot be compromised. The dataset consisted of 3,600 breast tumor photos that were divided into five categories: benign, malignant, cysts, fibroadenomas, and other nonmalignant tumors. Regarding the performance measures, the federated model achieved a 92% accuracy rate, 91% precision rate, 90% recall rate, and an F1 score of 90%. The outcome of this model is almost to a centralized model’s performance; it has an accuracy of 93 percent, with 92 percent precision, a recall of 91 percent, and an F1 score of 91 percent. The multiple advantages demonstrated by the federated learning technique include better data protection, the ability to utilize data from various sources belonging to different customers, and the reduction in the need for extensive centralized computations. However, we have identified a few challenges in this process, including the fact that there is often a need to over-communicate the process, the implementation process is complex, and the variation of performance due to data differences.

articleTitle: IoT-Assisted Indoor Air Quality Sensing and Predictive Analysis Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study on real-time Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) monitoring systems using different types of sensors in classrooms of an educational institute in Hyderabad. In this regard, an IoT model is proposed consisting of sensor nodes that capture different air pollutants concentrations such as CO2, CO, PM 2.5, PM 1.0, NO2, O3, and VOC including temperature and humidity sensors which affect air quality. The real-time data is collected for one month at various temperature levels and stored in the cloud. After transforming the real-time data into standard form, several ML-based classification models like Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Decision Tree (DT) are applied to analyze the real-time data where Random Forest outperforms other classification models providing an accuracy of 97.47%. Furthermore, two forecasting models i.e., ARIMA and LSTM models are applied to predict the concentration of air pollutants and compute the Indoor Air Quality Index (IAQI) level. It is viewed from the experimental study that the ARIMA model performs better than the LSTM model and it can be treated as a reference model to measure the IAQI level as it has been a requirement to check the pollution level in indoor classrooms after the COVID-19 pandemic.

articleTitle: Demystifying PDFs: Emerging AI for text generation and operation on PDF
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: AI is considered as most disruptive language and revolutionized various sectors with its ability analyze data with its large language model. incapability of other AI to read PDF and accept prompt and do text generation using their large language models .The work is based on proposing a new technique to integrate it into current AI. It will eliminate the need manual work of copy pasting Portable Document Format data to AI for prompt . In this can rely on Technologies Like Optical character recognition for reading images to text but challenging part is Portable Document Format to image and then image to text. this work is advancement of Optical character recognition which can eliminate the drawback of already existing technology.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Low Drop-Out Regulator with Integrated Current Sensor for Automatic Power Down in CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This presents a Low Drop-Out (LDO) Regulator featuring an integrated current sensor for automatic power down under no load conditions, implemented in a 0.18 μm CMOS process. The LDO regulator provides a stable 1.5 V output across a temperature range of -40 °C to 125 °C, operating from a supply voltage between 1.8 V and 2.2 V, and maintains stability with a load current range of 50 mA to 100 mA. The design achieves impressive line and load regulation values of 0.016 mV/V and 0.064 mV/mA, respectively. The inclusion of a power-down mechanism reduces power dissipation to 7.4523 μW under no load conditions. The architecture integrates three vital blocks: LDO, current sensor, and power down switch, with the current sensor accurately detecting load presence to trigger power down. Simulation results demonstrate the regulator's performance across different process corners, ensuring minimal power consumption and high efficiency, contributing to extended battery life in portable devices. This innovative design offers a significant advancement in energy-efficient power supply solutions for modern electronics.

articleTitle: Lightweight Scene Text Recognition Based on Knowledge Distillation and Transformer for Various Types of ID Cards
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: In recent years, photo-based ID recognition technology has been rapidly adopted by the banking and finance sector, driven by advances in digitalisation and artificial intelligence. These technologies allow customers to upload their IDs via mobile apps and the banking system automatically recognises and processes the information, reducing processing times and improving customer experience. But with this convenience comes the challenge of securing sensitive ID data. Traditionally, ID data has been transmitted to external servers, which increases the potential risk of data leakage and privacy exposure. Therefore, data security is becoming more important. In this research, we propose a novel lightweight model that combines knowledge distillation and transformer technology to achieve effective performance on different types of ID cards.

articleTitle: Advanced Computational Approaches in HR: Utilizing Neural Networks and Genetic Algorithms for Talent Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: Despite the constant changes within today’s Human Resources (HR) field, talent acquisition stands out as one of the most important strategic processes determining the performance of a company. The conventional recruiting approach is mostly performed and oftentimes proves to be time-consuming and non-inclusive. To address these challenges, this research focuses on the combination of intelligent technologies, namely neural networks and genetic algorithms in the context of talent acquisition. As a result, it was decided to use neural networks that have the best function for processing and analyzing massive unstructured information, such as resumes and job descriptions, to determine candidate suitability. Hypothesis 3 posited that since GAs are about optimization, multi-objective and were used to consider various factors at one time in the context of candidate job matching. As data sources, resumes of the IT employees, job descriptions of the positions, and employee performance analytics of this leading global technology company were used for the study. The CNN model needs to be further trained using other candidate sets of questions and achieve a screening accuracy of 85%, and an AUC-ROC score of 0.88 to properly screen candidates. The genetic algorithm model was also quite good with a classification accuracy of 82% and by using AUC-ROC it scored well 0.85. The best results employing both NNs and GAs indicated the highest performance measures; accuracy equal to 87%, precision equal to 85%, recall equal to 86%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.90. Such findings support the effectiveness of using both neural networks and genetic algorithms in redefining talent management by automating the process and reducing errors and prejudice in choosing talents. The implications for practical application for HR professionals and organizations are immense and identify that the use of these more complex computational methodologies can indeed provide a step up in recruiting performance. The study also shows that there is room for conducting more research to validate these models across industries and to work on the envisaged ethical issues regarding the use of AI in the field of HR.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-driven Quality Control Strategies for Industrial IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a new solution for improving Quality of Control in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems by using a machine learning approach. The planned system utilizes monitoring data originating from different sensors installed in the production line to detect faults as well as estimate maintenance requirements. Besides, the proposed system uses the state-of-art machine learning techniques like Convolutional Neural Networks for defect detection and Recurrent Neural Networks for Predictive maintenance with high accuracy and efficiency. Computer simulations indicate a high increase in the coverage of defects, predictive capability, and overall product quality. The combination of IoT and machine learning presents a convenient and evolutionary solution that becomes progressively enhanced as more data becomes available, and give a solid framework for the sustained optimization of standards in industrial practices. Future work seeks to enhance the developed models and extend the implemented system’s functionalities to other application domains and bigger data sets.

articleTitle: A Review on Transformer Models: Applications, Taxonomies, Open Issues and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: With each passing generation, the human language is getting rich vocabulary usually effected by regional, domain specific and emotional dialects. Natural Language Processing (NLP) deals with training machines the human context of verbal or textual expressions. Over the years transformers have played a crucial role in this regard with substantial advancement. Sequence to sequence (Seq2Seq) models advancements with the incorporation of attention mechanism helped in grasping relationship between different sequences for better understanding. The shortcomings of the model further surfaced giving way to amendments like pretraining on extensive datasets and using varied attention mechanism bringing into forefront of research Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT) models. Architectures based on Transformers have ventured strongly into the realm of generative modelling by classifying and understanding images-based data with models such as BERTvision, DALL-E and CLIP. Our analysis discusses the trajectory of Transformers. Current research endeavours emphasize on innovative designs, increased effectiveness, and expanded generalization capabilities. The discovery of Transformers represents a significant change in machine learning, since it enables models to understand intricate data across many modalities, hence improving the capabilities of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Change Detection in Agricultural Land using Satellite Generated Time Series Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
abstract: The land usage for agricultural activities is varying recently due to various changes taking place like urbanisation, industrialization etc. Observing the changes and monitoring the land usage for agriculture is crucial to meet the needs of the growing population. To better manage crops and bring more area under crops, information on the current status of change in crop areas must be known. Traditional methods of change detection often prove inadequate, necessitating a shift towards more advanced and data-driven approaches. The goal of this project is to design a novel application for change detection in agricultural land thereby to map and analyse the fluctuations and discrepancies involved in croplands of Davanagere. Remote sensing, particularly with satellite imagery, offers an effective means to detect and analyze changes in agricultural land in Davanagere region. The main objective of this project is to detect the land cover changes using satellite images for sustainable land cover planning in Davanagere region using Landsat-8 satellite images for a time period of 08 years from 2015 to 2022 considering the two season crop maps for alternate years.
